items.title: Exploitation minière illégale en Guinée : 10 ans requis contre 22 ex-administrateurs et 3 ans contre 202 orpailleurs étrangers
items.description: Le ministère public a requis, ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, de lourdes peines contre les 22 anciens administrateurs territoriaux de Siguiri et les 202 orpailleurs étrangers poursuivis dans le dossier des activités minières illégales dans cette préfecture. Devant la chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), le procureur spécial, Alphonse Charles Wright, a demandé 10 ans d’emprisonnement contre chacun des 22 anciens responsables administratifs et trois ans contre les 202 orpailleurs. Dans un premier temps, le procureur spécial s’est penché sur le dossier des 202 prévenus, principalement de nationalités burkinabè, malienne et togolaise. Ils sont poursuivis pour exploitation illégale des mines, dégradation de l’environnement, destructions diverses et pollution des eaux. Alphonse Charles Wright a soutenu que ces ressortissants étrangers ne disposaient d’aucune autorisation leur permettant de mener des activités minières dans la région de Siguiri. Il a rappelé que l’exploitation artisanale est réservée aux populations riveraines, dénonçant ainsi la présence de ces étrangers dans les zones minières. Pour étayer ses accusations, le procureur spécial a notamment évoqué leur interpellation en flagrant délit. « Les habits qu’ils portaient en prouvent éloquemment », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également dénoncé les conséquences environnementales de ces activités, citant l’assèchement des cours d’eau, les menaces pesant sur les activités agricoles ainsi que le manque de points d’abreuvement pour les animaux. Abordant ensuite le dossier des 22 anciens administrateurs territoriaux, poursuivis notamment pour leur implication présumée dans la facilitation des activités minières illégales, Alphonse Charles Wright a demandé à la Cour de retenir leur responsabilité dans l’installation et l’exploitation clandestines des sites miniers à Siguiri. Le procureur spécial a également sollicité que les faits de corruption soient retenus contre ces anciens responsables, tout en demandant leur relaxe du chef d’enrichissement illicite. Au terme de ses réquisitions, le ministère public a ainsi demandé trois ans d’emprisonnement contre chacun des 202 orpailleurs étrangers, en qualité d’auteurs principaux, et dix ans de prison contre chacun des 22 anciens administrateurs territoriaux. Il revient désormais à la Cour de se prononcer sur ces réquisitions.

items.title: At ECO moot, Dar calls for translating 'collective commitments into concrete action'
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, hosted the meeting under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”. The deputy premier, who chaired the meeting, expressed his “sincere appreciation to all delegations” for their constructive engagement during the meeting. “The deliberations today have reaffirmed our shared commitment to regional economic cooperation and integration,” Dar said. He termed the adoption of the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 an “important milestone in charting the future course of our organisation over the next decade”, saying that it provided a shared framework to advance regional priorities alongside the Islamabad Communiqué. “Our task now is to translate our collective commitments into concrete action,” he added. “This will require clear priorities, realistic timelines, and effective follow-up mechanisms.” He highlighted regional cooperation as a central pillar of Pakistan’s foreign policy and noted that the country had consistently advocated a “stronger, more effective and responsive” ECO that harnessed “geographical proximity, historical bonds and economic complementarities”. Dar underscored Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the ECO agenda as the chair of the organisation and to working with all institutions and member states to strengthen regional connectivity, facilitate intra-regional trade and promote mutually beneficial economic cooperation. He looked forward to welcoming the countries back for the 31st COM meeting in 2027, saying, “Let us build on the momentum generated here so that our next meeting can take stock of tangible progress in advancing our shared priorities.” In addition, he wished Iran success in hosting the upcoming 18th ECO summit on Dec 3-4. The deputy premier thanked all member states, as well as the secretary general and his team, ECO permanent representatives, and senior officials for their support. Later in the day, Dar held a media briefing on the meeting alongside ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. Araghchi calls for sustainable energy mechanism At the ECO meeting, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed the need for a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism during his address. The Iranian FM spoke about the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has also resulted in the choking of key fuel supply routes — the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab . “Our region needs not only an independent security framework but also a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism to safeguard energy flows, ensure stable supplies, reduce external vulnerabilities and enhance collective resilience against geopolitical shocks and disruptions,” Araghchi said, according to a transcript of his speech provided by the Iranian embassy in Pakistan. Araghchi said ECO was moving “beyond its traditional role towards becoming an effective platform for collective action, strengthened cooperation and joint efforts”. He said the shift would enable member states “to address emerging challenges and contribute to an inclusive and equitable global economic order”. He stressed the need for a “modern, new-generation, more inclusive, effective and operational trade agreement” that would benefit the region. Referring to the US war on Iran, Araghchi said, “Iran has remained committed to diplomatic engagement and peaceful solutions.” He added, however, that the US had opted for a different course of action, which was “marked by aggression, threats, targeted assassinations, economic coercion, and blockades, in flagrant violation of international law and the UN Charter”. He underscored that Iran had “no inherent dispute” with countries in the region, adding that “the territories, airspace and facilities of the regional countries must not be used as platforms for launching attacks against each other”. “Iran’s legitimate defensive measures are directed exclusively at the targets and military bases of the aggressors and should in no way be construed as actions against the peoples or governments of the neighbouring countries,” Araghchi said. He also called attention to Palestine , describing the genocide in Gaza as “the most pressing international crisis”. Condemning the destruction and killings at the hands of Israeli forces in Palestine, he said, “We are witnessing the intensification of expansionist policies by the Israeli regime in the West Bank and occupied Al-Quds.” “This is a moment that calls for concrete action, collective responsibility, and an end to silence and indifference.” He concluded his speech by reiterating that Iran’s stability and prosperity were “intrinsically linked” to those of other ECO members. ECO delegation heads call on PM Shehbaz Separately, the foreign ministers and delegation heads of ECO member states paid a joint call on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to a handout issued by the PM’s Office. The premier thanked them for their participation in the meeting and reaffirmed Pakistan’s “strong commitment” to ECO objectives. He reiterated his government’s resolve to promote regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration within the ECO member states. The premier appreciated the meeting’s successful conclusion and welcomed the adoption of the Islamabad Communique and the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035, describing them as “important steps” towards strengthening the organisation and advancing shared regional priorities. The premier highlighted Pakistan’s ECO chairmanship and emphasised the need to translate the organisation’s collective vision into concrete, result-oriented initiatives that deliver “tangible benefits” to the region’s people. Furthermore, the handout said that the premier called for enhanced cooperation in trade and investment, transport and transit connectivity, energy, information and communication technology, and sustainable development. “He stressed the importance of effective implementation of existing ECO agreements and strengthening institutional mechanisms to accelerate regional economic integration,” the statement said. PM Shehbaz highlighted the country’s strategic geographical location. He reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to enhancing regional connectivity through road, rail and multimodal transport corridors, including linkages with the ports of Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, to facilitate access to regional and international markets, particularly for landlocked ECO member states. “Underlining Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy for the peaceful resolution of disputes, the premier stressed the importance of collective efforts to address threats to regional security,” the statement added. He also expressed Pakistan’s resolve to work closely with all member states and the ECO secretariat to further strengthen the organisation during its chairmanship. “The prime minister reaffirmed that Pakistan looked forward to welcoming ECO member states again in 2027 for the next Council of Ministers Meeting and the ECO summit,” the handout concluded. Dar holds sideline meetings with participating dignitaries The deputy premier also held separate meetings with ministers from several countries attending the ECO moot. With FM Araghchi , Dar emphasised that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means of addressing outstanding issues, preventing escalation and achieving lasting peace and stability, the Foreign Office said. Meanwhile, Tajikistan’s FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin and Dar reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation within ECO and advancing its regional priorities. According to FO, the Tajik minister appreciated Pakistan’s warm hospitality. The two leaders “underscored the importance of realising the full potential of bilateral trade” and also discussed advancing energy cooperation, particularly through the early operationalisation of CASA-1000 . Dar and Turkiye’s Deputy FM Musa Kulaklikaya reaffirmed their “commitment to further strengthening the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood” between their countries, FO said. Dar thanked Türkiye for its active participation in the Council of Ministers meeting, while Kulaklikaya thanked Pakistan for the warm hospitality and arrangements for the meeting. In his meeting with Dar, Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy FM Kairat Tursunkulov delivered a letter from Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev, “reaffirming the close bonds of friendship and commitment to advancing bilateral ties”, FO said. The two sides discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and connectivity, and emphasised the importance of continued cooperation under ECO. Pakistan calls on Afghanistan to address terror concerns In his opening speech at the meeting, Dar said Pakistan desired a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan , but meaningful progress towards regional cooperation required the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism. He added that a stable Afghanistan, at peace with itself and all its neighbours and fully integrated into the ECO framework, would benefit the Afghan people as well as the wider region by opening up avenues for trade, transit and economic cooperation. “At the same time, meaningful progress requires the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of the neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism,” Dar said. He stressed that a secure and stable environment was essential for sustained regional economic partnerships, adding that these considerations remained central to Pakistan’s broader connectivity agenda. “Regional connectivity rests on more than the routes that link us. It depends upon trust between states and confidence that international commitments will be honoured. Unresolved disputes and the non-fulfilment of international obligations can erode that trust and impede economic progress,” said Dar. The foreign minister emphasised that respect for international law and treaties is essential to enduring economic partnerships between countries. Outlining Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship of the ECO, Dar identified five key areas of focus, including expanding trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, advancing the ECO Trade Agreement, building regional resilience and promoting human development. The foreign minister said the region’s natural resources, energy reserves, agricultural potential and strategic location offered considerable opportunities for economic cooperation, but realising that potential required functioning transport corridors, efficient border procedures and predictable transit arrangements. He said Pakistan would work towards wider market access, stronger regional value chains and greater private sector participation, particularly by small and medium-sized enterprises, to boost trade and investment among member states. “Closer interaction among our business communities can help translate commercial potential into greater trade and investment.” Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in a cordial exchange with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Tajikistan Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, OIC Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed and ECO Secretary General Dr. Asad Majeed Khan on the sidelines of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting in Islamabad on Nov 16. — ForeignOfficePk/X On connectivity, Dar said Pakistan would seek to improve transport and transit links between Central Asia, South Asia and Pakistani ports on the Arabian Sea. Harmonised customs procedures, efficient border management and predictable transit arrangements were essential to making regional trade routes commercially viable, he added. The foreign minister also highlighted the need to advance the ECO Trade Agreement, saying the negotiating strategy and roadmap approved by ECO trade ministers in November 2025 provided a basis for modernising the agreement. Pakistan would support efforts to develop a more effective, inclusive and digitally enabled regional trade framework, he said. On regional resilience, Dar called for closer cooperation in disaster preparedness, early warning systems, sustainable water management and climate-resilient infrastructure, noting that climate change and growing pressure on water and energy resources posed serious challenges to regional economies. He also underscored the importance of human development, particularly in education, research, innovation and vocational training, saying greater opportunities in these areas could equip young people with skills needed by changing economies. Promoting entrepreneurship and professional exchanges would further strengthen regional integration, he added. The foreign minister maintained that the five priorities were interconnected and their success would depend on collective efforts by member states. He expressed Pakistan’s readiness to work with ECO members and the organisation’s secretariat on initiatives relating to trade facilitation, transit connectivity and disaster preparedness. Regional peace and diplomatic efforts Dar cautioned that peace and stability were essential for economic development, warning that conflict and insecurity in the region could disrupt trade routes, energy supplies, investment and economic projects. “Peace and development reinforce each other,” he said. He added that Pakistan remained “deeply concerned about conflict and instability” in the region. “Their consequences extend beyond national boundaries, disrupting trade routes, energy supplies, investment, and the economic projects of our peoples.” He said that Pakistan has consistently advocated for “the peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter”. Referring to Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the US-Israeli war on Iran, Dar said, “Pakistan will continue these diplomatic efforts in support of dialogue, de-escalation, and lasting regional stability.” He said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir “remained closely engaged with brotherly countries and international partners to facilitate peaceful outcomes”. Senior officials meet to finalise agenda Senior officials of the ECO finalised the agenda and draft Islamabad Communiqué on Sunday, ahead of the organisation’s COM meeting. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), the Senior Officials Meeting (SOM) was held on Nov 15 under the chairmanship of Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad. The meeting was attended by senior officials from ECO member states, representatives of the ECO Secretariat, and delegates from the organisation’s specialised agencies and regional institutions. The officials reviewed preparations for the ministerial meeting and finalised its agenda and the draft Islamabad Communiqué for consideration by the foreign ministers. They also reviewed the activities undertaken by the ECO Secretariat during the year, including ongoing programmes and initiatives, outcomes of sectoral ministerial meetings, and the work of subsidiary bodies and specialised institutions, the ministry said. Administrative and financial matters of the organisation also came under discussion, with participants exchanging views on measures to improve its effectiveness. The SOM serves as a preparatory forum for the ECO COM, enabling member states to assess progress, discuss issues of mutual interest and build consensus on proposals and draft documents ahead of ministerial-level deliberations.

items.title: Tchad: une évasion fait deux morts, 30 détenus en cavale
items.description: La maison d’arrêt de Mongo, dans la province du Guéra au Tchad, a été le théâtre d’une évasion, le dimanche 15 novembre 2026. Selon un bilan provisoire des autorités, l’incident a fait deux morts et trois blessés graves. Trente prisonniers sont toujours recherchés, tandis que plusieurs infrastructures et documents administratifs ont été détruits. La maison d’arrêt de Mongo, dans le centre du Tchad, a connu une évasion aux conséquences meurtrières, le dimanche 15 novembre 2026. Le bilan provisoire fait état de deux décès et de trois blessés graves. Trente détenus ont réussi à prendre la fuite, selon les autorités locales. Les chiffres ont été communiqués par le délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province du Guéra, le général Abdoulaye Ibrahim Siam, et le procureur général près la Cour d’appel de Mongo, Djouma Mahamadene. Le décompte des prisonniers, réalisé cellule par cellule, a permis de recenser 476 détenus sur un total de 510 personnes officiellement enregistrées. Cette opération a ainsi révélé un manque de 34 prisonniers, dont 30 sont formellement signalés en fuite. Au-delà des pertes en vies humaines, l’évasion a provoqué d’importantes destructions au sein de l’établissement pénitentiaire. Six bureaux, notamment ceux de la direction, du secrétariat, de la surveillance et de la sécurité, ont été ravagés par les flammes. Le magasin de stockage et la pharmacie ont également été saccagés, avec à la clé la destruction de médicaments. Les dégâts concernent aussi les archives de la prison. Les registres d’écrou et de levée d’écrou, indispensables au suivi administratif des détenus, ont été entièrement détruits. D'autres biens ont été perdus, notamment 25 cartons d’ustensiles, 100 moustiquaires récemment offertes par l’UNICEF ainsi que des machines à coudre endommagées. Cet épisode vient raviver le souvenir d'une précédente crise dans cette même prison. En avril 2025, une mutinerie y avait déjà fait quatre morts, témoignant des tensions récurrentes qui secouent l’établissement. Réputée comme l’une des prisons les plus redoutées du Tchad, après celle de Koro-Toro, située dans le nord du pays, la maison d’arrêt de Mongo fait face à une surpopulation chronique et à des conditions de détention particulièrement éprouvantes. Une situation qui place une nouvelle fois cet établissement pénitentiaire au cœur des préoccupations sécuritaires et carcérales du pays. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Tchad: une évasion fait deux morts, 30 détenus en cavale est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Former Sudanese minister assaulted during armed robbery in Uganda
items.description: Sudanese journalist and former Minister of Information Faisal Mohammed Saleh and photojournalist Sari Omer were assaulted during an armed robbery in Uganda’s capital, Kampala, on Saturday. The two men were attacked by gunmen in central Kampala, who beat them, threatened them and stole their belongings, according to reports from Sudanese media. Saleh and Omer were taken to hospital with cuts, bruises and minor injuries. They received medical treatment and were later discharged. Ugandan police have reportedly opened an investigation into the attack and are working to identify those responsible. There is currently no indication that the attack was politically motivated, and it has so far been reported as an armed robbery. items.title: INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has dismissed as false and misleading a viral social media video alleging that the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) would be remotely logged out before the end of voting. The commission clarified that only the poll official operating the device has the authority to log in or log out of the BVAS during voter accreditation and the subsequent result upload process. INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its official X platform on Monday, following the circulation of a video on Instagram alleging that voters would be logged out of the system before the conclusion of voting. Describing the claim as fabricated, the commission said each polling unit was assigned unique login credentials, which were issued to the Presiding Officer on the eve of an election. According to INEC, the credentials enable the poll official to log into the BVAS for voter accreditation on election day and subsequently upload the polling unit result sheet at the close of polls. “The claim that the BVAS can be remotely logged out before the conclusion of accreditation and voting is false,” the commission stated. It stressed that there was no provision for any external individual or authority to remotely log out the device. The commission also dismissed claims that election results uploaded offline could be lost, explaining that the IReV application had been upgraded to accommodate offline uploads. INEC said the enhancement followed experiences during the 2023 general election, when some poll officials were held hostage at their polling units because they could not upload results due to poor or non-existent network connectivity. It explained that the offline upload feature allows poll officials in areas with poor or no network coverage to upload polling unit result sheets in the presence of stakeholders at the polling unit. According to the commission, such results remain securely stored on the BVAS pending successful transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). ” As Poll Officials proceed from the polling unit to the Ward Collation Centre and the device reconnects to the internet, the result sheet is automatically transmitted to the IReV portal without requiring any further manual intervention,” it said. INEC assured Nigerians that the BVAS and IReV systems operate in accordance with established procedures designed to protect the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process. The commission urged members of the public to disregard the video, refrain from creating or sharing unverified information and rely on its official communication channels for accurate information. It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the conduct of free, fair and credible elections. The post INEC debunks claim of remote BVAS log-out before voting ends appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cinkassé/taekwondo : huit pratiquants en examen de passage aux grades supérieurs
items.description: Cinkassé, 16 nov. (ATOP) – La Fédération togolaise de taekwondo (FTTKD) a organisé, le dimanche 15 novembre à Cinkassé, un examen de passage de grades ayant permis à huit postulants de concourir pour l’obtention des ceintures noires des 1 er , 2 è et 4 è dan. La délégation de la FTTKD, composée du maître Djondo Jean Médard, secrétaire général adjoint de la fédération et ceinture noire 5 è dan et du maître Dégboé Joselito, ceinture noire 7 è dan, arbitre et juge technique international, a évalué les huit candidats, dont deux filles, venus de Kara, Dapaong et Cinkassé, à l’issue de trois jours de stage préparatoire. Parmi eux, deux postulaient au 1 er dan, trois au 2 è dan et trois au 4 è dan. Les candidats ont été soumis à huit épreuves portant notamment sur les mouvements de base, le combat imaginaire contre plusieurs adversaires, la self-défense, l’attaque-défense, la casse de planches, l’enchaînement de coups de pied, le combat et une épreuve orale. Le maître Dégboé Joselito a félicité les postulants pour leur détermination et leur courage. Il leur a rappelé les principes et les valeurs du taekwondo, notamment la discipline, l’intégrité, le respect, la courtoisie, la combativité et l’esprit indomptable. Des candidats, membres de la délégation et autorités locales Le président du comité d’organisation de l’examen, le maître Akpayi Kpatcha Richard, a salué la FTTKD pour le choix porté sur Cinkassé pour abriter cet événement. Il a réaffirmé son engagement à œuvrer pour le développement du taekwondo dans la région des Savanes. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Cinkassé, Koutob Tsapou, a salué le courage ainsi que le dévouement des postulants. Il a réitéré le soutien des autorités locales aux initiatives de promotion du taekwondo dans la préfecture. L’examen a été précédé d’un stage de trois jours, à la fin duquel les candidats ont soutenu leurs mémoires. Les résultats de cet examen seront proclamés dans deux semaines. ATOP/BB/JK/AR

items.title: NACOC arrests 5th suspect over 2,600kg cocaine seizure in Spain
items.description: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested a fifth suspect in connection with the seizure of approximately 2,600 kilogrammes of cocaine in Valencia, Spain, bringing the number of suspects in custody to five. The Commission disclosed this in a statement signed by its Public Affairs and International Relations Directorate, announcing the latest development in its investigations into the international drug trafficking operation. It identified the five suspects as Safura Bashiru, 43; Mahouda Alhassan, 48; Altaher Abdel Karim Maiga, 25; Mint Dahamane Badria, 39; and Konare Cheick Oumar, 38. NACOC said the arrests followed months of surveillance, intelligence gathering and coordinated operations by its officers. According to the Commission, all five suspects are currently in custody as investigations continue to uncover other individuals connected to the shipment. It said the probe had been intensified to identify and apprehend other accomplices, including those who may have been involved in financing, coordinating and providing logistical support for the trafficking operation. The Commission said it was working to establish the full extent of the network and bring all those involved to justice. It further reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening intelligence-led enforcement and international cooperation to prevent drug trafficking networks from using Ghana as a transit point for illicit narcotics. “The fight against drug trafficking remains relentless, and there will be no haven for those engaged in this criminal enterprise,” NACOC stated. The Commission assured the public and its international partners of its continued resolve to dismantle drug trafficking networks through sustained enforcement and intelligence-sharing efforts.

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : clôture dans le rouge
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a clôturé dans le rouge lundi, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,63% à 17.239,53 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, s'est stabilisé à 1.272,47 pts, alors que le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a lâché 0,98% à 1.302,62 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a, quant à lui, abandonné 0,28% à 1.640,42 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Mines » (-4,75%), « Sylviculture et papier » (-3,51%) et « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (-3,15%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Télécommunications » (+1,12%), « Électricité » (+0,77%) et « Services de transport » (+0,53%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Le volume global des échanges a dépassé 511,03 millions de dirhams (MDH), dominées par Attijariwafa bank (31,52 MDH), Managem (25,78 MDH) et SODEP-Marsa Maroc (17,35 MDH). Pour sa part, la capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 1.006,78 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Jet Energy (+19,97% à 171,55 DH), Maroc Leasing (+2,57% à 359 DH), BMCI (+2,31% à 562,7 DH), Jet Contractors (+1,79% à 1.650 DH) et Auto Hall (+1,68% à 59,99 DH) ont affiché les plus fortes hausses. À l'inverse, Zellidja (-7,46% à 259,1 DH), Managem (-5,14% à 1.366 DH), Stroc Industrie (-3,89% à 153 DH), Med Paper (-3,51% à 22 DH) et S.M. Monétique (-3,45% à 473,1 DH) ont accusé les plus forts replis. The post Bourse de Casablanca : clôture dans le rouge appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Diabète : 60 MMDH de coût annuel, pourquoi le Maroc doit investir dans la prévention, selon Dr Hamdi
items.description: Avec près de trois millions d’adultes atteints et une proportion importante de malades qui ignorent leur état, le diabète constitue un défi sanitaire autant qu’économique pour le Maroc. Pour le Dr Tayeb Hamdi, médecin et chercheur en politiques et systèmes de santé et vice-président de la Fédération nationale de la santé (FNS), l’urgence est de réorienter les dépenses vers le dépistage précoce et la prévention, alors que le coût économique et social de la maladie est estimé à 3,8 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB). Toutes les cinq à six minutes, un nouveau cas de diabète est diagnostiqué au Maroc. Derrière ce rythme de progression se dessine une réalité qui dépasse largement le cadre des consultations médicales et de la prise en charge thérapeutique. Avec près de trois millions d'adultes concernés, selon les estimations internationales, la maladie chronique pèse sur les finances publiques, fragilise les ménages et menace, à terme, la soutenabilité du système de protection sociale. Le diabète est ainsi devenu, selon le Dr Tayeb Hamdi, « une question de santé publique, de protection sociale et de développement économique ». Dans une analyse livrée à Hespress FR , Dr Hamdi souligné que le premier obstacle tient à la difficulté de repérer les personnes atteintes. Dans son communiqué du 14 novembre 2026, le ministère de la santé et de la protection sociale reprend les résultats de l'enquête nationale STEPS, réalisée en 2017-2018, qui établissait la prévalence du diabète à 10,6 % chez les adultes âgés de 18 ans et plus. Cela correspond à environ 2,7 millions de personnes. Près de la moitié d'entre elles ignoreraient leur maladie. À cette population s'ajoutent les personnes présentant un état de prédiabète, estimées à 10,4 % des adultes, ainsi que plus de 43.000 enfants atteints de diabète, notamment de type 1. Les données de la Fédération internationale du diabète (FID) confirment l'ampleur du phénomène. Son dernier Atlas estime à 2,881 millions le nombre de personnes âgées de 20 à 79 ans vivant avec un diabète au Maroc en 2024, avec une prévalence standardisée sur l'âge de 11,9 %. Ces chiffres, issus de méthodes et de populations de référence différentes, convergent vers un même constat : le pays doit faire face à une maladie largement répandue, dont une partie des personnes concernées ne bénéficie pas encore d'un diagnostic. Pour le Dr Hamdi, le défi est donc double : identifier les personnes qui s'ignorent diabétiques, puis garantir à celles dont le diagnostic est établi une prise en charge régulière, efficace et financièrement accessible. Car un diagnostic tardif augmente le risque de complications et alourdit considérablement la facture sanitaire. Une facture qui dépasse largement les remboursements de l'assurance maladie Le coût du diabète ne saurait être réduit aux dépenses consacrées aux médicaments et aux consultations. La maladie entraîne des complications parfois lourdes, parmi lesquelles l'insuffisance rénale, le recours à la dialyse, les maladies cardiovasculaires, la cécité, les amputations et les handicaps. À ces dépenses médicales directes s'ajoutent les arrêts de travail, les pertes de productivité, les décès prématurés et les charges financières supportées par les proches. Cette distinction entre coûts directs et indirects est essentielle pour mesurer l'impact réel de la maladie. Les premiers comprennent notamment les médicaments, l'insuline, les consommables médicaux, les consultations, les examens, les hospitalisations et les traitements des complications. Les seconds renvoient aux conséquences économiques et sociales de la dégradation de l'état de santé : incapacité à travailler, baisse de productivité, perte de revenus et appauvrissement des ménages. Les chiffres disponibles illustrent l'écart entre les dépenses enregistrées par les organismes de couverture médicale et le coût sanitaire global du diabète. Selon les données de l'Agence nationale de l'assurance maladie (ANAM) pour 2021, reprises par le ministère de la santé, les dépenses annuelles de santé associées à cette maladie dépassaient 1,5 milliard de dirhams. Un montant déjà considérable, mais qui ne reflète pas l'ensemble des ressources mobilisées par la maladie. La Fédération internationale du diabète estime, pour sa part, à 1,3075 milliard de dollars les dépenses de santé imputables au diabète au Maroc en 2024. Cette évaluation repose sur un périmètre sanitaire international plus large que celui des seuls remboursements d'un régime national d'assurance maladie. Les deux données ne recouvrent donc pas exactement le même champ et ne peuvent être directement assimilées. L'impact devient encore plus important lorsque sont intégrées les conséquences indirectes de la maladie. Une étude scientifique publiée en juillet 2025 dans l' Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal , revue de l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS), évalue le coût économique et social du diabète au Maroc à l'équivalent de 3,8 % du PIB national en 2023. Cette proportion représente un ordre de grandeur de 56 milliards de dirhams pour cette année-là et d'environ 60 milliards de dirhams en 2025. Cette estimation, fondée sur une modélisation internationale, prend en compte non seulement les dépenses médicales, mais également les pertes de productivité, les incapacités et la valorisation économique des décès prématurés. Une estimation plus restrictive, fondée sur un périmètre de coûts réduit, aboutit à un montant inférieur d'environ 75 %, selon les éléments avancés par le Dr Hamdi. L'écart entre les dépenses sanitaires directes et le coût économique global révèle ainsi une dimension souvent sous-estimée du diabète. La maladie ne mobilise pas uniquement les ressources du système de santé : elle affecte également la capacité des individus à travailler, les revenus des familles et, plus largement, la production de richesse nationale. Réorienter les dépenses vers la prévention Face à cette situation, le Dr Tayeb Hamdi plaide pour une révision de la logique de financement du système de santé. Plutôt que de concentrer l'essentiel des ressources sur le traitement des complications, il estime nécessaire d'investir davantage en amont, dans le dépistage, la prévention et le suivi régulier des patients. « Nous devons passer d'un système qui finance principalement les complications à un système qui finance davantage leur prévention », résume-t-il. Cette réorientation suppose, en premier lieu, de renforcer le dépistage ciblé dans les structures de soins de santé primaires. Les personnes présentant des facteurs de risque, notamment celles vivant avec une obésité, une hypertension artérielle ou ayant des antécédents familiaux de diabète, devraient pouvoir bénéficier d'un dépistage précoce et d'un accès simplifié aux examens nécessaires pour confirmer le diagnostic. L'enjeu ne s'arrête toutefois pas à l'identification des malades. Une prise en charge efficace nécessite un parcours de soins continu, associant éducation thérapeutique, disponibilité régulière des médicaments, accès aux examens de suivi et orientation rapide vers les structures spécialisées lorsque des complications apparaissent. Le médecin insiste également sur la nécessité d'une meilleure articulation entre les secteurs public et privé, afin d'éviter les ruptures dans le suivi et de garantir une continuité des soins. Le financement de ces prestations constitue l'autre volet de sa proposition. Le Dr Hamdi réitère ainsi une recommandation qu'il défend depuis plusieurs années : instaurer, dans le cadre de l'Assurance maladie obligatoire (AMO), un forfait national de prévention sans avance de frais. Ce dispositif couvrirait notamment le dépistage du diabète et de l'hypertension, le suivi de certaines maladies chroniques ainsi que des consultations préventives. L'objectif serait de supprimer les obstacles financiers susceptibles de retarder le recours aux soins, en particulier pour les populations les plus vulnérables. « La prise en charge intégrale des prestations préventives essentielles, accompagnée d'une évaluation médico-économique, peut constituer un levier de protection financière », estime le chercheur. Une telle approche permettrait de rendre le dépistage réellement accessible, tout en limitant les dépenses ultérieures liées aux complications évitables. Pour le médecin, il ne s'agit donc pas simplement d'augmenter les budgets consacrés à la santé, mais de modifier leur affectation. Détecter plus tôt, traiter efficacement et réduire le reste à charge des patients sont autant de moyens de préserver les ressources des familles, de consolider la pérennité de l'assurance maladie et de protéger le potentiel économique du pays. Surpoids et obésité, un front de prévention dès l'enfance Cette stratégie ne peut cependant se limiter au dépistage et au traitement. Elle doit également s'attaquer aux facteurs qui favorisent la progression du diabète de type 2, au premier rang desquels figurent le surpoids et l'obésité. Cette forme de diabète est étroitement associée à l'obésité, notamment abdominale, à la sédentarité, à l'âge et aux prédispositions génétiques. Le Dr Hamdi rappelle toutefois que le surpoids n'explique pas toutes les formes de diabète et que le diabète de type 1 obéit à des mécanismes différents. La prévention ne doit donc pas se transformer en culpabilisation des personnes atteintes. Les données nationales et internationales témoignent néanmoins de l'importance du problème. L'enquête STEPS de 2017-2018 évaluait à environ 53 % la proportion d'adultes en surpoids, obésité comprise, au Maroc. La prévalence de l'obésité était alors estimée à 20 %. Dans ses projections modélisées pour 2025, la World Obesity Federation porte à 59 % la proportion d'adultes en surpoids ou obèses, soit près de six adultes sur dix. Un adulte marocain sur quatre souffrirait désormais d'obésité selon ces estimations. Pour le chercheur, la lutte contre le diabète doit par conséquent s'inscrire dans une politique plus large de prévention des maladies chroniques, engagée dès l'enfance. Elle implique une action coordonnée entre les secteurs de la santé, de l'éducation, de l'alimentation et de l'aménagement de l'environnement. L'école constitue notamment un espace privilégié pour installer précocement des habitudes favorables à la santé. L'accès à une alimentation équilibrée, la limitation de la consommation de boissons sucrées et la promotion de l'activité physique doivent être accompagnés d'un environnement quotidien qui facilite les choix les plus sains. Cela passe aussi par des espaces urbains adaptés à la marche et à l'activité physique. Au-delà des comportements individuels, cette approche suppose donc des politiques publiques capables de rendre les modes de vie favorables à la santé plus accessibles. La prévention de l'obésité ne peut reposer uniquement sur la responsabilité des individus lorsque l'offre alimentaire, les conditions de vie et l'organisation des villes influencent également les habitudes. Le constat défendu par le Dr Tayeb Hamdi est finalement celui d'un décalage entre le coût considérable du diabète et la place encore insuffisante accordée à sa prévention. Avec une facture économique et sociale évaluée à près de 3,8 % du PIB, la maladie représente un enjeu qui engage bien davantage que le seul système de soins. « La prévention du diabète est un investissement dans la santé des Marocains, mais également dans l'avenir économique et social de notre pays », souligne-t-il. Une équation qui invite à considérer le dépistage précoce, la continuité des traitements et la protection financière des patients non comme des dépenses supplémentaires, mais comme des investissements susceptibles de limiter, à terme, une facture sanitaire et économique bien plus lourde. The post Diabète : 60 MMDH de coût annuel, pourquoi le Maroc doit investir dans la prévention, selon Dr Hamdi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Plateau State Government has raised concerns over the growing burden of diabetes in the state, following the record of 5,457 suspected new cases between January and September 2026. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Monday during a press briefing in Jos to commemorate the 2026 World Diabetes Day. Ba’amlong said the figure followed 5,546 suspected cases recorded in 2025, but clarified that the numbers represented suspected cases and not confirmed diagnoses. He said diabetes remained a major public health concern because many people were living with the condition without knowing their status. The commissioner also disclosed that findings from the 2024 nationwide Know Your Number, Control Your Number screening campaign showed that 14,359 people were screened in Plateau State, with 2,610, representing approximately 18 per cent, recording elevated blood glucose levels. He, however, cautioned that the findings did not represent the prevalence of diabetes in the state. According to him, the figures underscore the need to expand access to screening, diagnosis and treatment services. As part of activities marking this year’s World Diabetes Day, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with the Plateau State chapters of the Diabetes Association of Nigeria and the Endocrine and Metabolic Society of Nigeria, conducted a free workplace screening exercise at the Joseph Gomwalk Secretariat Complex, Jos. Ba’amlong said the exercise targeted 1,000 civil servants and provided blood glucose and blood pressure checks, weight and body mass index assessments, health education, counselling and referrals for further medical attention where necessary. Speaking on government interventions, the commissioner said the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang was working towards extending diabetes education and screening services to underserved communities across the state’s 17 local government areas through existing primary healthcare facilities and community outreach programmes. He added that the government was exploring partnerships and appropriate medical technologies to improve access to diagnostic services, particularly at the primary healthcare level, while strengthening follow-up and referral systems for people with elevated blood glucose levels. “Screening is only the beginning. Early detection must lead to appropriate diagnosis and treatment,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, particularly those with a family history of diabetes, excess weight or high blood pressure, to check their blood glucose levels regularly and seek medical attention when necessary. He also advised residents to adopt healthy lifestyles through balanced diets, regular physical activity and weight management, while avoiding tobacco and limiting alcohol consumption. Ba’amlong identified excessive thirst, frequent urination, unexplained weight loss and persistent fatigue as some of the symptoms that could indicate diabetes. He further urged people living with the condition to adhere to prescribed treatment and attend regular medical reviews to prevent complications. World Diabetes Day is observed annually on November 14 to raise awareness about diabetes, promote prevention and encourage access to quality healthcare for people living with the condition. The post Plateau records 5,457 suspected diabetes cases in nine months appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dar says Pakistan to host next Makkah alliance summit later this month
items.description: Pakistan will host the next meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance’s apex committee, likely later this month, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday. He made the remarks while answering a query during a press briefing regarding a ministerial meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) held in Islamabad. Asked about regional security architecture, Dar recalled the Aug 7 signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The pact empowers the three states to treat an attack on any one of them as an attack on all. Providing details on the alliance’s progress, Dar noted that its apex committee, called the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC), “will actually be meeting, hopefully [at the] end of this month, in Islamabad”. “We offered in our inaugural meeting that our next formal meeting will be held in Islamabad and everybody accepted,” he said, noting that an emergency meeting of the SPDC was held in Riyadh last month amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The SPDC comprises the foreign and defence ministers of the three countries, as well as their top military officials. In response to the question about a possible new security architecture for the region, Dar said: “Well, let me be very honest with you. I think time and again, different regions, including this region, have witnessed that the need and the best way to have regional security is to have some sort of security at the local or domestic architecture. “In other words, this region should have its own security architecture. Maybe this is a beginning.” He remarked that the “global institutions who claim to be masters of having the security arrangement globally were not created in one day”, adding that the Makkah pact was signed for self-defence. The foreign minister highlighted that the pact does not violate Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, which allows individual and collective defence. “Now, it is not restricted that these three countries will have a monopoly and will not have, will not entertain ever [any] other membership,” he said. DPM Dar said there was a “transition time of setting up the infrastructure” of the alliance, as part of which various decisions were made, including related to the secretary general’s office and the permanent secretariat in Riyadh. He added that a working committee has also been formed, comprising one person each from the foreign, defence and military offices of the three countries. “That committee has been working; it has had a few sessions. And the last meeting, hopefully, will be in November, where they will work out all the nitty-gritty regarding detailed SOPs etc,” he said. “I’m very hopeful that, God willing, this is not going to benefit just these three countries. New membership will be entertained after we are established in about one year,” Dar further said, adding that membership requests of those who will agree to the alliance’s principles will be entertained. ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar were also present at the media briefing. Islamabad has ‘not given up’ on US-Iran peace efforts DPM Dar also reaffirmed that Islamabad has not given up on its diplomatic efforts for a peaceful resolution to the US-Iran war. Replying to a query, Dar said he had “very candid, very frank, very brotherly, very comprehensive discussions” with Iran’s FM Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the ECO meeting, which they both attended. Noting that the two discussed the latest regional situation, the deputy premier said Iran had “fast-tracked” its seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to a two-day plan . “So, the response from the United States is pending. We have not given up hope or efforts. We are still doing our best [so] that the situation gets sorted out,” DPM Dar stated. He also expressed hope that, now that Washington was no longer busy with its midterm elections, it would respond to the proposal “very soon”. Asked how ECO planned to navigate the US sanctions on Iran, considering that the organisation’s secretariat was based in Tehran , Dar said, “Sanctions are not going to be there forever. “And once sanctions are over, the whole world will just land there; I can guarantee,” he maintained, recalling that a British prime minister was the first person to visit Tripoli when sanctions against Libya were withdrawn. “I think the legal side, the sanctions, international abiding of the sanctions … Pakistan has always, you know, followed international law, UN Charter and followed whatever resolutions have been decided and adopted in the UN Security Council,” Dar affirmed. He expressed his hope that the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding signed between Iran and the US on June 18 was implemented. Dar remarked that the seven-day and two-day Hormuz proposals were “actually extracted” from the Islamabad MoU. “There’s nothing new. It’s only fast-tracking things here and there, showing confidence-building measures, taking actions by one side and opening of the Hormuz by the other. “So I think let’s hope for the best. We haven’t given up hope,” the foreign minister reiterated. In their meeting on the sidelines, Dar and Araghchi reviewed bilateral relations and exchanged views on regional and international developments of mutual interest, the Foreign Office (FO) said. “They reaffirmed the strong and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Iran and reiterated their commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation through sustained high-level engagement.” According to FO, Araghchi congratulated Pakistan on the successful hosting of the ECO ministers’ meeting and “appreciated the productive deliberations, warm hospitality and excellent arrangements”. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to advancing ECO’s priorities, particularly regional cooperation and connectivity, the statement added. On his part, Dar emphasised that “dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means of addressing outstanding issues, preventing escalation and achieving lasting peace and stability”. Stressing the value of continued engagement and consultations, both sides agreed to maintain close contact on matters of mutual interest. Months of diplomacy have failed to resolve the war, which began with surprise US-Israeli strikes on Tehran that assassinated Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. During more than eight months of war, Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a key oil trade route — and struck infrastructure and US assets across the Middle East. On Sunday , Bahrain was rattled by the second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the war. On Friday, following this month’s US strikes on Qeshm island in Hormuz, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said their forces had targeted a US early warning radar system in Bahrain.

items.title: Ejiofor hails DSS DG over evacuation of Igbo youths from Wawa facility
items.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Human rights lawyer, Sir Ifeanyi Ejiofor, has commended the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, for reforms at the Wawa detention facility and the evacuation of a significant number of Igbo youths from the facility. Ejiofor also praised Ajayi for what he described as an end to the alleged arbitrary arrest and abduction of Igbo youths, which he claimed had become frequent under the previous leadership of the Service. The lawyer made the commendation in a statement on Monday titled, “Wawa Barracks: The horrifying testimonies of survivors of enforced disappearances under the Buhari regime — a time for Igbos to introspect”. He expressed concern over alleged abuses at the detention facility, including arbitrary arrests, torture, deprivation of medical attention and deaths, based on accounts he attributed to former detainees. According to him, the situation had at some point deteriorated to the extent that some individuals of Igbo extraction allegedly exploited security agencies to settle personal scores. He said the reported reforms under Ajayi had helped restore confidence and a measure of security in the South-East. “Happily, that dark chapter has been brought to an end, restoring confidence, peace and a measure of security in the South-East geopolitical zone,” he said. Ejiofor described the alleged experiences of detainees as disturbing, claiming that many Igbo youths had suffered under the previous DSS leadership. He, however, stressed that his criticism of alleged security abuses should not be interpreted as support for criminal activities by non-state actors operating in the region. ” No grievance, however genuine, confers a licence for criminality; equally, no allegation of criminality confers a licence for lawlessness by the State,” he said. The lawyer appealed to the DSS Director-General to facilitate the release of more detainees who, according to him, had no involvement in criminal activities and against whom there was no credible evidence of wrongdoing. He also urged the Service to withdraw charges allegedly founded on ethnic profiling, arguing that addressing the underlying causes of agitation was more important than sustaining what he described as prejudicial ethnic categorisation. Ejiofor further commended Ajayi for what he called commendable reforms within the Service, saying the intervention demonstrated the importance of professionalism and institutional changes in rebuilding public confidence. He called for an end to the use of propaganda as a security strategy, arguing that public trust could only be restored through justice, accountability and respect for citizens’ rights. The lawyer also urged the Igbo people to reflect on the crisis, warning against internal divisions and the exploitation of collective grievances by individuals seeking personal benefits. He said the community should not allow the alleged misconduct of others to become an excuse for internal wrongdoing or personal vendettas. Ejiofor also accused the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari of overseeing a pattern of abuses against Igbo youths, alleging that the former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, and former DSS Director-General, Yusuf Magaji Bichi, played significant roles. He said recent testimonies by alleged survivors of detention at Wawa Barracks had brought to light claims of physical torture, psychological trauma, denial of medical care and deaths in custody. According to him, some detainees reportedly survived on inadequate food and water, with conditions worsening before the change in DSS leadership under the Tinubu administration. He further claimed that the new leadership had initiated changes, including the release of some detainees against whom no indictments were sustained, the payment of compensation without court orders and the transfer of some detainees to conventional custodial facilities. Ejiofor maintained that the reforms should be sustained, while calling for the release of other detainees against whom no credible evidence of criminal wrongdoing existed. items.title: Ghana Swim League returns for Season 5 as two new clubs make debut
items.description: The Ghana Swim League made its much-anticipated comeback on Saturday, November 2026, with Season 5 at Meet 1, at the Borteyman Sports Complex. The opener, which set the tone for a new season, saw various swimmers from across the country gathered at the Aquatic Center at Borteyman to battle in several strokes, and a strong start to the six-meet regular season. One of the biggest turning points of Meet 1 was the debut of two new sim clubs; WaveOn Aquatics and Aspire Swim Club, a clear sign of the League’s continued growth since its launch in November 2022. Their arrival expands the field of participating teams to 14 for the new season, including established powerhouses like GH Dolphins, Marlins, Tema Seals, Ghana Bluefins, Legon Swimming Club, Lincoln Community School, The Monarchy Swimming Academy, Torpedo Swim Club, Aquatic Masters, African Sharks, Blue Whales and Dolphin Swim Center, who eventually missed out at Meet 1. Besides, the GSL Season 5 at Meet 1 brought together both male and female swimmers to compete in 16 individual and team events, comprising of Girls and Boys 50m Breaststroke, Girls and Boys 50m Butterfly, Girls and Boys 100m Backstroke, Girls and Boys 9 and Over 200 Freestyle, Girls and Boys 9 and Over 200m IM (Individual Medley), Girls and Boys 10 and Under 200m Freestyle Relay, Girls and Boys 11-14 400m Freestyle Relay and Girls and Boys 15 and Over 400m Freestyle Relay. Participating swim clubs include, African Sharks, Blue Whales, Dolphins Swim Center, GH Aquatic Masters, Ghana Bluefins Swim Club, Ghana Dolphins, Legon Swimming Club, Lincoln Community School, Marlins Swim Team, Tema Seals Swim Team, The Monarch Swimming Academy, Torpedo Swim Club with Alraad Swim School and Club Asen both missing out. The two-day swimming championship took place from Saturday, June 13 to Sunday, June 14, 2026. Ghana Dolphins are into Season 5 as the team to beat after a dominant run in Season 4. The Dolphins won the Meet of Champions 2026, claiming the ultimate title for three consecutive seasons out of four. Some top male swimmers; Marlins’ Michael Arthur Crabbe-Mann, Jonathan Forcados of Legon Sharks, and Kelvin Abdallah of GH Dolphins, all missed out at Meet 1 of Season 5 as Abeiku Jackson, Ghana’s two-time Olympian made entry at the season opener. In the female category, Oduma Agyei from GH Dolphins made a late entry at the Meet 1 as team mate Mercedes Abdallah was unavailable due to her involvement at the Youth Olympic Dakar 2026 in Senegal alongside her brother, Kelvin Abdallah. Speaking to Ermines Onyema, official announcer of the Swim League, Kojo Abbiw Jackson, Director of the Ghana Swim League was upbeat that the league is still ascending despite successes chalked and expressed excitement following the brilliant debut of WaveOn Aquatics and Aspire Swim Club. Meanwhile, the league action for Meet 2 of the GSL Season 5 bounces back on December 5, 2026, and will run to 1st May, 2027, all at the Borteyman Sports Complex before climaxing with the Meet of Champions on 12th and 13th June, 2027.

items.title: Ghana’s 2027 Budget: From macroeconomic stability to prioritising public investment
items.description: The 2027 Budget presents a consequential change in Ghana’s fiscal priorities: having restored a measure of macroeconomic stability, the government is committing considerably more resources to productive public investment. It is a direction I welcome. But the achievement of the New Economy cannot ultimately be judged by the size of its capital budget. Its success must be measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment and productivity—and on those outcomes, the jury is still out. Before the Budget, I raised three questions: How much of the additional fiscal space would be devoted to new public investment? How would the government finance the programme? And how would it reconcile an ambitious reserve-accumulation agenda with urgent investment needs? The Budget offers satisfactory answers to all three. A stronger platform for investment The 2026 economic outturn supports the government’s claim that stabilisation has advanced. Real GDP grew 6.2% in the first half of 2026; headline inflation was 5.5% in October. During January–October, the commitment-basis primary surplus reached 1.4% of GDP, and the cash deficit was 2.3% of GDP against a programmed 4.5%. Public debt stood at 47.5% of GDP at end-October. Average commercial-bank lending rates had fallen to about 15.9%, while private-sector credit was expanding at 34% year on year in September. These developments suggest that Ghana’s macroeconomic conditions are generally moving in a favorable direction, providing a stronger foundation for sustained economic stability and growth. The next task is different from stabilisation: translating improved prices, debt dynamics and financial conditions into higher productive capacity and better livelihoods. The Budget makes public investment an explicit priority The original indicative 2027 framework provided GH¢82.8 billion—4.6% of GDP—for capital expenditure including capital transfers. Appendix 3A of the final Budget raises that allocation to approximately GH¢122.7 billion, or 6.8% of GDP. That is nearly GH¢40 billion more than I original indication, and above the illustrative 6.1%-of-GDP investment benchmark I discussed before the Budget. This is a credible signal of intended additional investment, although genuine additionality ultimately depends on project-level execution. The historical comparison places the decision in perspective: the proposed 6.8% capital allocation is the highest in this 2016–2027 series, reversing a slide from 6.7% in 2016 to 3.6% in 2025. It tells us about a change in fiscal intent, not yet about economic returns. The change is also apparent relative to debt service. The budget allocates GH¢100.4 billion in direct capital expenditure for 2027, against GH¢61.0 billion in interest payments—a ratio of approximately 1.65. For comparison, the 2025 historical outturn was approximately 0.41. In other words, the 2027 Budget proposes allocating roughly GH¢1.65 to direct capital expenditure for each cedi in interest payments.

items.title: Quizz SONAGESS : 23 heureux gagnants repartent avec plusieurs lots
items.description: La Société nationale de gestion du stock de sécurité (SONAGESS), à travers le Projet d’appui à la gestion du stock d’intervention (PAGSI), a procédé ce lundi 16 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à la remise des prix aux gagnants du quiz SONAGESS, un concours lancé dans le cadre de la promotion de la consommation locale. À travers cette initiative, la SONAGESS entend se rapprocher davantage des populations et mieux faire connaître ses missions et ses actions en faveur de la sécurité alimentaire. Lancé le 27 octobre et clôturé le 31 octobre 2026, le jeu consistait à répondre à cinq questions par jour portant sur le PAGSI et la SONAGESS. Selon le chargé du projet PAGSI, Jacob Ouédraogo, chaque publication a enregistré plus de 200 commentaires durant les cinq jours de compétition. Les cinq premiers participants ayant fourni les bonnes réponses étaient retenus pour être récompensés quotidiennement. Un des heureux gagnant du quiz recevant sont prix A en croire le chargé du projet PAGSI, cette initiative visait notamment à mesurer le niveau de connaissance des populations sur les actions menées par la SONAGESS, leur impact sur le quotidien des bénéficiaires ainsi que les services proposés par la structure à travers le PAGSI. Il s'agissait également dit-il, de faire connaître les produits locaux mis à la disposition des populations. Au terme du jeu, 23 gagnants ont été enregistrés sur les 25 initialement attendus, deux questions n'ayant pas reçu de bonnes réponses. Pour Côme Nikièma, l'un des heureux gagnants du quiz, cette initiative constitue une occasion de découvrir davantage les produits issus de la production nationale.T Ayant découvert la publication de la SONAGESS alors qu'il scrollait sur Facebook, Côme affirme avoir tenté sa chance au deuxième quiz, dont la question portait sur le nom du directeur général de la société et l’année de sa nomination. Jacob Ouédraogo, Chargé du projet PAGSI « C’est une réelle satisfaction de faire partie des gagnants. Cela me permet aussi de vraiment déguster les saveurs burkinabè » s’est-il réjoui. Côme Nikièma a par ailleurs salué l’initiative et encouragé la SONAGESS à multiplier ce type d’activités afin de permettre aux populations de mieux connaître ses actions et les efforts déployés par l’État en faveur de la sécurité alimentaire. Côme et les 22 autre gagnants repartent chacun avec des lots composés notamment d’un tee-shirt à l’effigie de la SONAGESS, d’un sac de cinq kilogrammes de riz et d’un sac de cinq kilogrammes de maïs. Une vue des lots Créé en 2022, le projet PAGSI vise à améliorer la disponibilité des aliments de qualité à travers l'accroissement des quantités collectées ainsi que l'accessibilité financière et physique des populations vulnérables aux denrées alimentaires. À travers ce jeu concours, la SONAGESS entend donc contribuer à la promotion de la production nationale et à l'adoption du principe du « consommons local » dans les habitudes quotidiennes des populations. Sidziguin Irène Corinne SAWADOGO Minute.bf

items.title: Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya tells govt
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kwankwasiyya Movement has accused the Kano State Government of politicising the reported attack on the convoy of its leader, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, insisting that the state belongs to all residents, irrespective of their political affiliations. The movement said the government had a responsibility to protect all citizens and should not allow political differences to undermine their safety and fundamental rights. Its spokesperson, Dr Habibu Sale Mohammed, stated this in a statement on Monday while reacting to the reported attack on Kwankwaso’s convoy during a political engagement in Bichi Local Government Area on Sunday. The movement also criticised the state government for dismissing the incident as fictitious and accusing the Kwankwasiyya Movement of fabricating the allegation to attract public sympathy. It specifically faulted the Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, for demanding pictures and videos of the incident rather than allowing security agencies to investigate the allegation. The group questioned why victims should be expected to provide evidence before the government could express concern about their safety. “Kano belongs to all its people, not exclusively to those occupying government offices. Its security, peace and democratic freedoms are collective responsibilities that must never be sacrificed on the altar of partisan politics,” the statement said. The movement maintained that investigating allegations of criminal activities was the responsibility of security agencies, not the victims. It also accused the commissioner of reaching conclusions on the incident without presenting the outcome of any police investigation. The group called on the Kano State Police Command to investigate the reported attack, establish what transpired in Bichi and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. It further demanded an investigation into the alleged destruction of vehicles and injuries reportedly sustained by members of Kwankwaso’s delegation. The movement urged Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to rise above political considerations and guarantee the safety of all political parties, candidates, campaign officials and supporters across the state. It warned against political intimidation, insisting that opposition members must be allowed to participate in lawful political activities without fear of harassment or violence. “Political competition is not warfare, and opposition politics is not a criminal offence,” the statement added. The Kwankwasiyya Movement said it remained committed to peaceful political participation but warned that its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for acceptance of intimidation or impunity. It urged the state government to allow security agencies to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident before making public statements on the matter. The post Kano belongs to all, not those in power, Kwankwasiyya tells govt appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kintinian : l’interdiction de l’orpaillage provoque un exode massif et paralyse les activités économiques et scolaires
items.description: L’interdiction de l’orpaillage artisanal dans la préfecture de Bouré-Kintinian provoque un départ massif des travailleurs allogènes vers leurs localités d’origine. Ce mouvement de population inédit paralyse désormais la vie économique et entraîne la fermeture de plusieurs écoles de statuts différents dans les zones minières. Depuis l’entrée en vigueur de cette mesure d’interdiction, la situation sur le terrain suscite une vive inquiétude. Les gares routières des localités sont prises d’assaut. De nombreux véhicules stationnent aux alentours pour assurer le transport des voyageurs contraints de plier bagage dans l’urgence. Les conséquences de cet exode sont immédiates et visibles dans toutes les zones minières de la préfecture de Kintinian. Le départ massif des orpailleurs a vidé les lieux de commerce de leurs clients habituels, poussant les vendeurs à baisser rideau. L’impact sur l’éducation est également palpable : plusieurs établissements scolaires ont fermé leurs portes. Les enfants des travailleurs déplacés sont contraints d’interrompre leur année scolaire pour suivre leurs parents. Lors d’un micro-trottoir réalisé dans les différentes gares routières de la place, la détresse était palpable sur les visages. Bien que les parcours soient différents, les témoignages recueillis convergent vers les mêmes préoccupations majeures. Les voyageurs affirment quitter les zones minières à contrecœur, privés de leur unique source de revenus pour subvenir aux besoins de leurs familles. De nombreux parents déplorent cette situation brutale qui compromet l’avenir scolaire de leurs enfants, obligés de quitter les bancs de l’école en plein cursus. Pour ces travailleurs habitués à percevoir un revenu journalier, rester une ou deux semaines sans descendre dans les mines rend la prise en charge quotidienne extrêmement difficile. D’une seule voix, les travailleurs lancent un plaidoyer à l’endroit du président de la République et de son gouvernement afin d’obtenir une reprise rapide des activités minières. Parmi ces voyageurs en détresse, le témoignage de Bintou Condé, mère de sept (7) enfants, illustre la précarité soudaine dans laquelle se trouvent de nombreuses familles : « Je reside à Kintinian dépuis quinze (15) ans avec mon mari. Je venais à peine de subir une intervention chirurgicale, il ya moins de deux (2) semaines, lorsque cette crise à éclaté avec l'arrêt immédiat des activités minières. Face à la présence massive des dispositifs des forces de sécurité, mon mari a dû fuir en brousse et m'a contrainte à partir. Pourtant, je suis encore soufrante et nous n'avons rien. Aujourd'hui, je retourne chez moi à Kissidougou bien malgré moi. Je démande pardon au président de la république Mamadi Doumbouya, et à son gouvernement: qu'ils aient pitié de nous, et autorisent la reprise des travaux, car nous souffrons énormement. » Face à cette montée de la tension sociale et à l’impatience des travailleurs, les autorités locales tentent de rassurer. Le maire de la commune a récemment pris la parole au nom des autorités compétentes pour informer l’opinion publique que les négociations avancent à grands pas. L’objectif affiché par l’État est de parvenir à une reprise encadrée et réglementée de l’orpaillage artisanal. Toutefois, entre l’impératif pour les autorités de mieux structurer et sécuriser le secteur minier et l’urgence économique des populations qui vivent au jour le jour, le défi reste entier. Les prochains jours seront déterminants pour trouver un équilibre capable de relancer l’économie locale tout en garantissant le retour des élèves en classe. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Kintinian : l’interdiction de l’orpaillage provoque un exode massif et paralyse les activités économiques et scolaires est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: Shehu Buba inaugurates 1,000-member campaign council
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The governorship candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) in Bauchi State, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, has inaugurated a 1,000-member campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging members to embrace unity, peaceful political engagement and issue-based campaigns. Buba, who represents Bauchi South Senatorial District in the National Assembly, inaugurated the council on Sunday, with members drawn from the 20 local government areas of the state. He described the inauguration as a major step towards strengthening the party’s grassroots mobilisation, coordinating its political activities and improving its chances in the 2027 governorship election. The senator said the council comprised experienced party stakeholders and directors representing the various senatorial districts and local government areas, with the responsibility of developing strategies and coordinating campaign activities. He urged members to set aside personal differences and work collectively towards the party’s victory, stressing that political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, persuasion and mutual understanding. Buba warned against violence, slander and character assassination, insisting that electoral victory could only be achieved through constructive engagement with voters and the presentation of credible alternatives. He said his ambition to govern Bauchi State was driven by the desire to address what he described as challenges of misgovernance and redirect the state towards sustainable development and prosperity. According to him, his development agenda will focus on economic stability and growth, improved security, urban and rural infrastructure, people-oriented reforms and the general welfare of residents. The PRP candidate also emphasised the importance of grassroots mobilisation, adequate electoral preparation and voter education, particularly on the need for voters to protect their votes after casting their ballots. He noted that effective governance would require cooperation between the executive and legislative arms of government, expressing the need for the PRP to secure representation in the State House of Assembly and National Assembly to facilitate the implementation of its manifesto. Describing the 2027 contest as challenging, Buba charged members of the campaign council to develop a workable programme and adopt strategies capable of securing victory for the party. He urged them to take the campaign to communities, wards and polling units, listen to residents’ concerns and communicate the party’s programmes and policies to the electorate. He further insisted that the PRP’s campaign should be guided by respect for voters and issue-based engagement rather than unnecessary attacks on political opponents. Expressing confidence in the party’s chances, Buba identified unity, commitment, hard work and popular support as critical factors for victory. He subsequently declared the campaign council inaugurated and directed members to commence immediate grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns and engagements across the state. Earlier, the Bauchi State Chairman of the PRP, Abdulrahman Yusuf Muazu, said the campaign council was carefully constituted to reflect the political composition and diversity of the state. He urged members to regard their appointments as a privilege rather than a mark of superiority over other party faithful, warning against complacency, indiscipline and arrogance. Muazu charged them to work diligently towards attracting more members and supporters to the party ahead of the elections. Also speaking, the Director-General of the campaign council, Hon. Ibrahim Makama, assured that the council was ready to commence mobilisation and campaign activities to build support for the PRP and its governorship candidate. Makama described his appointment and those of other members as a privilege, pledging their loyalty and commitment to the party’s objectives and Buba’s governorship ambition. He also urged party members and supporters to conduct issue-based campaigns, shunning character assassination, calumny and violence.
