items.title: 2027: Tinubu, Oborevwori assured of victory in Delta — Olejeme
items.description: By Precious Enaike The Zonal Director, South-South Election Planning, Coordination, Monitoring and Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dr. Ngozi Olejeme, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu, Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates will win the 2027 general elections. Olejeme attributed her optimism to what she described as the growing strength of grassroots mobilisation within the party’s campaign structure, particularly in Oshimili South Local Government Area of Delta State. She spoke at the Oshimili South Arcade, Asaba, where she joined other party leaders in welcoming Oborevwori, his deputy, Sir Monday Onyeme, former Governor Ifeanyi Okowa and other members of the State Campaign Council to the local government. The former boss of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) assured the governor that her council was prepared to mobilise support for all APC candidates in the area. Addressing party supporters, traders, youths and other residents at the rally, Olejeme expressed confidence that sustained grassroots engagement would translate into overwhelming electoral support for the APC. She said, “My Governor, we are here to tell you that Tinubu has already won. All APC candidates have already won. Mr. Governor, Oshimili South is the capital of government, and we trust and believe in you. “Based on the work we have done so far at the grassroots, I can assure you that we have already delivered President Tinubu and you, our confirmed Governor.” Olejeme, however, urged residents and party supporters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), stressing that grassroots mobilisation must be backed by active participation in the electoral process. “I have only one request to make: Go and make sure you collect your PVC. Your PVC is what will give us this victory. Collect your PVC; it is very important because we are already set for victory. We have reached our promised land, and your PVC is of immense importance at this point,” she said. She described Oborevwori as a performing governor who had exceeded expectations, while applauding Tinubu for what she called his achievements in office. Olejeme urged Nigerians to give the President another mandate in 2027, arguing that his performance deserved a second term. “Our Governor has performed very well. Governor Oborevwori is the best in Africa. President Tinubu has done so much that the people are not talking about. For the good work he has done, we have to give him more work to do by re-electing him in the 2027 general election,” she said. She expressed confidence that Tinubu, Oborevwori, senators and other APC candidates would emerge victorious in the 2027 elections. items.title: Tinubu’s debt interest exceeds revenue, NDC alleges
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of plunging the country into what it described as “fiscal suicide”, alleging that interest payments on public debt have exceeded the Federal Government’s total revenue. The party claimed that Nigeria spent N7.7 trillion on debt interest payments in the first half of 2026, compared with total federal revenue of N6.2 trillion, representing 124.19 per cent of revenue generated within the period. The NDC Spokesperson for the National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, made the allegations in a statement issued on Monday ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to the party, the figures, which it attributed to the World Bank’s 2026 Nigeria Development Update, indicate that the country is increasingly borrowing to service existing debts rather than investing in critical infrastructure and social services. It said the development had placed an additional burden on Nigerians and threatened the economic prospects of future generations. The statement read, “The grim reality for every suffering family in our nation today is that under the President Bola Tinubu administration, Nigeria is no longer borrowing to build roads, equip hospitals, or fund schools. It is borrowing recklessly to pay interest on past debts, thereby mortgaging the survival of today’s citizens and the destiny of unborn generations.” The party further claimed that debt interest payments rose from N5.6 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N7.7 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, consuming 3.1 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). It contrasted the figure with capital expenditure, which it said fell to N700 billion, representing 0.3 per cent of GDP, from one per cent in the corresponding period of the previous year. Describing the disparity as alarming, the NDC said the government was spending about 11 times more on debt interest than on critical infrastructure. The party also faulted the administration’s revenue performance, arguing that the increase in federal revenue from N3.6 trillion to N6.2 trillion had not translated into improved living conditions for Nigerians. It attributed the revenue growth to increased taxation and pressure on businesses and ordinary citizens, alleging that much of the money was being channelled into servicing high-cost domestic borrowing. The NDC also referenced the recurring question raised by its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, over the utilisation of funds accruing to the country following the removal of petrol subsidy and increased borrowing. “This reckless trajectory is unsustainable,” the party declared. It consequently called for an immediate halt to what it described as reckless domestic borrowing, a comprehensive audit and restructuring of the country’s debts, and a review of government spending priorities. The party also advocated increased investment in infrastructure, healthcare, education and productive sectors, alongside a reduction in government overheads. Looking ahead to the 2027 elections, Ikokwu expressed confidence that the Obi/Kwankwaso presidential ticket would offer Nigerians an alternative built on productivity, fiscal discipline and sustainable economic growth. She said an NDC-led government would prioritise the responsible management of public resources and redirect spending towards areas capable of improving citizens’ welfare and strengthening the economy. items.title: Niger : la Cour des comptes alerte sur la gestion de la société publique des eaux
items.description: La gestion de la Nigerienne des Eaux (NDE), societe publique creee pour succeder a la Societe d'exploitation des eaux du Niger (SEEN), est severement mise en cause dans un rapport provisoire de la Cour des comptes date de juillet 2026. Portant sur 2023 et 2024, le document, dont des donnees avaient ete publiees le 13 novembre par le site Le canard dechaîne , recense 154 constats relatifs a la transition, a la gouvernance, aux finances et a la qualite de l'eau. Selon la Cour, la transition n'a pas ete suffisamment encadree : aucun bilan consolide de cloture ni etat contradictoire du patrimoine n'aurait ete etabli. Les comptes de la SEEN a fin 2023 n'ont pas ete certifies et le bilan d'ouverture de la NDE repose sur des donnees provisoires. Des immobilisations evaluees a 4,11 milliards de FCFA et des stocks de 2,67 milliards auraient ete transferes sans inventaire contradictoire exhaustif. Le rapport releve l'absence d'outils de gouvernance, dont un plan strategique, un manuel de procedures et une fonction d'audit interne operationnelle. Des decisions financieres depassant sept milliards de FCFA auraient ete executees sans approbation prealable des tutelles. La Cour signale aussi l'utilisation de quinze comptes bancaires ouverts au nom de la SEEN, plus de sept milliards de FCFA d'operations en suspens a fin 2024 et des irregularites dans les marches publics. Des analyses de l'eau preoccupantes Les constats les plus sensibles concernent la qualite de l'eau. La Cour indique avoir analyse 54 echantillons physico-chimiques et 54 echantillons microbiologiques dans six regions : Dosso, Tahoua, Maradi, Zinder, Tillaberi et Niamey. Les resultats font etat d'une contamination microbiologique importante. Les coliformes totaux atteindraient 50 100 UFC/100 ml a Dogondoutchi et 30 200 a Maradi, alors que la valeur de reference est de zero. Le document releve des insuffisances de chloration, des pompes doseuses en panne ou mal utilisees et l'absence de chlore residuel a certains points du reseau. a Maradi, les teneurs en nitrates mesurees en laboratoire atteindraient 392,5 a 708,8 mg/l, pour une norme nigerienne de 45 mg/l. Des depassements sont aussi signales a Say, Zinder et Dogondoutchi. La Cour mentionne des reactifs perimes, un manque d'equipements de mesure et l'absence de releves reguliers. La vetuste de canalisations favoriserait les fuites et les infiltrations d'eaux usees. Ces defaillances exposeraient les populations a des maladies hydriques, dont les diarrhees, la typhoïde, la dysenterie et le cholera, selon le rapport, qui appelle a des mesures correctives immediates. Une societe financierement fragilisee La Cour estime que le modele economique de la NDE reste fragile, notamment en raison de creances clients de 14,01 milliards de FCFA et de depenses insuffisantes pour la qualite du service et la maintenance. Ces faiblesses pourraient compromettre la viabilite de la societe et la continuite du service public. Les conclusions restent provisoires. Les responsables concernes disposent d'un mois pour repondre aux observations, fournir des justificatifs ou contester certains constats. Le rapport definitif sera arrete apres examen de ces reponses. Le document ne constitue donc pas, a ce stade, une decision definitive etablissant leur responsabilite.

items.title: 2027: Don’t trade children’s future for money, Lamido tells Jigawa women
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Jigawa State, Mustapha Sule Lamido, has urged women to reject monetary inducements from politicians ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against sacrificing their children’s future for temporary financial gains. Lamido made the appeal while addressing PDP stakeholders during meetings in Gumel and Hadejia, where he urged women to consider the long-term implications of their electoral choices. He cautioned against accepting money and other material gifts from politicians at the expense of the future of their children, urging voters to critically assess the performance of the incumbent administration before deciding which party to support. The PDP candidate said the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government should be judged by its record in office rather than campaign promises, propaganda or alleged attempts to influence voters through the distribution of money and other items. Lamido maintained that the PDP had a record of achievements from its previous administrations to present to the electorate, insisting that the party was better positioned to offer the state an alternative direction. He urged voters to evaluate whether the APC-led administration had met their expectations, adding that those dissatisfied with its performance should consider the PDP as an alternative in 2027. He stressed that the future of Jigawa State and the well-being of the next generation should take precedence over temporary political benefits. The post 2027: Don’t trade children’s future for money, Lamido tells Jigawa women appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Engins de chantier : Pour les SEM Days, NEEMBA Burkina met en avant les équipements SEM et ouvre un showroom SEM à Gampèla
items.description: Les SEM Days 2026 ont été lancés ce jeudi 5 novembre sur le site de NEEMBA Burkina, à Gampèla, dans la commune de Saaba. Organisées jusqu’au 6 novembre, ces journées offrent aux professionnels du bâtiment, des travaux publics, des mines et des carrières l’occasion de découvrir les équipements de la marque SEM, d’assister à des démonstrations et d’échanger avec les équipes techniques et commerciales de l’entreprise. Au-delà de la présentation des engins, cette rencontre constitue un cadre d'échanges autour des besoins des entreprises et des solutions susceptibles de contribuer à la réalisation de leurs projets. Le programme comprend notamment des démonstrations de machines, des conseils techniques et commerciaux, ainsi que des possibilités de financement proposées avec les partenaires financiers présents sur le site. Pour Emir Sanoh, Directeur Pays de NEEMBA Burkina, l’organisation des SEM Days répond à la volonté de rapprocher les équipements des professionnels et de leur permettre de mieux apprécier leurs capacités. « Les SEM Days, c’est l’occasion de réunir l’ensemble de nos partenaires et des entreprises dans un cadre concret » , a-t-il expliqué. Une gamme d’équipements adaptée aux besoins des chantiers-©Faso7 Au cours de ces deux journées, les visiteurs peuvent découvrir plusieurs catégories d’équipements SEM, notamment des chargeuses, des bulldozers, des niveleuses, des tombereaux et des compacteurs. Des pelles figurent également parmi les équipements annoncés pour compléter prochainement l’offre présentée au Burkina Faso. Intégrée à l’écosystème industriel de Caterpillar, la marque SEM propose des équipements destinés aux travaux de terrassement, de compactage, de manutention et de construction. Son offre s’accompagne de services visant à assurer le suivi des équipements, notamment en matière de maintenance et de disponibilité des pièces de rechange. Selon Osborn IGBOKWE, Business Developer SEM au sein du réseau NEEMBA, ces journées constituent une opportunité de rapprocher les équipements des acteurs locaux. Elles permettent aux professionnels de découvrir les machines, d’obtenir des réponses à leurs préoccupations et d’identifier les solutions les mieux adaptées à leurs projets. Un accompagnement au-delà de la vente d’équipements-©Faso7 Au-delà de la présentation des machines, NEEMBA Burkina entend mettre l’accent sur le suivi des équipements pendant leur cycle de vie. L’entreprise veut notamment accompagner ses clients dans le choix du matériel, son entretien et le maintien de sa disponibilité sur les chantiers. « Notre ambition, c’est de ne tenir aucune barrière dans la communication entre nous pour que nous puissions être présents lorsqu’ils en ont besoin » , a déclaré Emir SANOH, signifiant sa volonté de renforcer la proximité avec les clients. A son niveau, Isaac YAMEOGO, Responsable commercial chez NEEMBA Burkina, a insisté sur l’accompagnement proposé aux acquéreurs des équipements SEM. Il a notamment évoqué la disponibilité du service après-vente, des pièces de rechange, de techniciens qualifiés et la possibilité d’effectuer des interventions directement sur les chantiers. Il a également souligné l’existence de partenariats avec des institutions financières pour accompagner les entreprises dans le financement de leurs projets d’acquisition. « Si vous avez un projet, nous pouvons le porter ensemble avec nos partenaires financiers » , a-t-il assuré, avant d’inviter les professionnels à s’intéresser aux machines SEM. Placées sous le haut parrainage du Camarade Mikaïlou SIDIBE, ministre de la Construction de la Patrie et le co-parrainage du Camarade Yacouba Zabré GOUBA, ministre de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, les SEM Days se sont poursuivies jusqu’au vendredi 6 novembre 2026. Les professionnels intéressés ont pu profiter de cette dernière journée pour découvrir les équipements et échanger avec les équipes de NEEMBA Burkina. items.title: Achievements of ‘New Economy’ must be measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment and productivity – Dr. Nsafoah
items.description: A US-based Assistant Professor of Economics at Niagara University, Dr. Dennis Nsafoah, wants the success of the New Economy measured by sustained improvements in economic growth, employment, and productivity. According to him, the New Economy cannot ultimately be judged by the size of its capital budget. Before the 2027 Budget, he raised three questions: How much of the additional fiscal space would be devoted to new public investment? How would the government finance the programme? And how would it reconcile an ambitious reserve-accumulation agenda with urgent investment needs? According to him, the budget offers satisfactory answers to all three. In his commentary on the budget titled “Ghana’s 2027 Budget: From Macroeconomic Stability to Prioritising Public Investment”, Dr. Nsafoah said the 2027 Budget identifies a markedly larger public investment envelope, communicates a mainly domestic financing strategy and offers a measured formal reserve-adequacy benchmark. “These are reasons for a constructive assessment, not a guarantee of success”. Dr. Nsafoah, who is also a member of the Board of Tesah Capital also said the most consequential risk is the capacity to finance new investments while repeatedly refinancing the inherited stock of domestic obligations at sustainable cost. “That risk deserves monitoring, but not alarmism”, he pointed out. “Ultimately, I will judge the New Economy by whether Ghana produces more per worker, attracts additional private investment, creates durable jobs and achieves sustained growth—not by how large the capital budget appears on presentation day. The government has made a promising allocation choice. The economic verdict must follow the results”, he explained. Financing the New Economy: Domestic Borrowing and Its Implications The government in the 2027 Budget clearly identified how it intends to finance the New Economy programme. The 2027 cash deficit is budgeted at GH¢65.8 billion (3.6% of Gross Domestic Product), with GH¢85.0 billion in net domestic financing and GH¢17.7 billion in net external repayments. In effect, Dr. Nsafoah said the domestic markets will fund both the fiscal deficit and the net repayment to foreign creditors, highlighting that the budget projects GH¢59.0 billion in net financing from commercial banks and GH¢25.9 billion from non-bank investors. He stressed that limited new external borrowing reduces exposure to new foreign-currency debt, but places greater demands on domestic financial intermediation. He added that the more important concern is the government’s gross financing requirement and the associated refinancing risk, rather than the GH¢85 billion in net domestic borrowing alone. “Beyond financing new expenditure, the government must also repay or refinance maturing Treasury bills and other domestic debt obligations. Ghana’s substantial stock of short-term government securities, together with significant debt maturities scheduled for 2027 and 2028, creates additional pressure on domestic financial markets”, he warned. Consequently, he said the government’s ability to sustain its investment programme will depend partly on its capacity to manage these refinancing obligations while maintaining favourable borrowing conditions.

items.title: No casualty as gas explosion rocks Lagos NNPC station, spreads to school
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni A gas explosion on Sunday rocked a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggering a fire that spread to the adjoining Saint Lawrence Greater Height School. No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1pm, as the school was closed for the weekend. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the fire was successfully contained through the prompt intervention of firefighters. Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50pm and arrived at the scene at 1:13pm. She disclosed that firefighters from Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were deployed to the scene to combat the fire, prevent further damage and bring the situation under control. According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly to the adjoining school, affecting parts of its premises. She, however, said the firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school. “No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated. She added that preliminary investigations into the cause of the explosion were ongoing. items.title: Trump says he might meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China
items.description: United States President Donald Trump said on Monday he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China this week, an announcement that could dramatically reshape his upcoming trip through East Asia if it occurs. The president, who met the North Korean leader several times during his 2017-2021 term, including once in the Korean Demilitarised Zone , has previously expressed interest in another meeting during his current term. Senior US officials, however, have previously said he has no immediate plans to do so. Moreover, Trump has repeatedly previewed meetings with Kim that never took place, including during a trip to Asia last year. North Korea, whose mission to the United Nations did not immediately respond to a request for comment, has publicly indicated it has no intention of meeting with the US president at this time. Trump told reporters while departing the White House en route to the Philippines and China that any meeting would occur in China, and that Kim’s presence was ultimately up to Chinese President Xi Jinping. “[Xi] was here a month ago, and we’re also going to meet with [Russian] President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also,” Trump said. “So that’ll be good. We have a chance to accomplish a lot.” Trump has indicated he will meet with Putin and Xi during his trip , but US officials and analysts have played down the possibility of a meaningful agreement emerging from any trilateral sit-down. Among the possible topics of conversation , Trump and others have said, are Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, counterproliferation and the war in Iran.

items.title: Methane cuts offer cheap, fast route to tackling global warming – UN climate chief
items.description: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell has urged governments to accelerate efforts to cut methane and other super-polluting greenhouse gases, describing the measures as among the fastest, cheapest and most effective ways to slow global warming in the near term. Addressing the Leaders-Level Non-CO₂ Greenhouse Gases Summit at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 12, 2026, Mr Stiell said reducing methane emissions could deliver immediate climate benefits while improving public health, boosting agricultural production and generating significant economic returns. He said climate-related disasters were already destroying lives, disrupting livelihoods and contributing to inflation, warning that the consequences would worsen as global temperatures continue to rise. “In a world of suffocating disasters, action on methane offers breathing space,” he said. Mr Stiell said reducing methane and other super pollutants was essential to limiting near-term temperature increases and ensuring that any overshoot of the 1.5°C global warming threshold remained as short and limited as possible. He, however, stressed that methane reductions must be accompanied by rapid cuts in carbon dioxide emissions to prevent further increases in global temperatures. Existing technologies can deliver significant methane cuts Mr Stiell identified the oil and gas, solid waste and agricultural sectors as major sources of methane emissions, noting that existing technologies could significantly reduce their contribution to global warming. He said approximately 70 per cent of methane emissions from the oil and gas sector could be eliminated using existing technologies, with much of the reduction achievable at low or no net cost. In the solid waste sector, he said, 75 per cent of methane reduction measures could generate financial savings, with the economic value of captured methane potentially exceeding the investment required to implement the solutions. He argued that accelerating the deployment of these technologies would deliver benefits beyond climate mitigation, including improved energy efficiency, cleaner air, better agricultural yields, lower costs and fewer deaths. Citing findings by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition, Mr Stiell said every dollar invested in key super-pollutant solutions could generate $15 in economic gains alone. “The business case is absolutely clear,” he said. He also highlighted the economic losses associated with gas flaring, revealing that approximately 167 billion cubic metres of gas were flared annually during oil and gas production, representing an estimated $54 billion in lost energy value. “And that’s money going up in smoke,” he said. Countries urged to translate climate commitments into action Mr Stiell said international recognition of the importance of methane reduction was growing, with more than 90 per cent of parties, representing approximately three-quarters of global methane emissions, having included measures to cut methane in their new Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). He said the priority must now shift from making commitments to implementing them. “The task now is to turn those plans into action,” he said. He identified COP31 as an opportunity to advance practical solutions and strengthen international momentum, including through methane and waste targets being pursued by the COP31 Presidency. He also highlighted the Super Pollutant Country Action Accelerator as an initiative designed to provide countries with the support needed to advance their emissions-reduction efforts. Stiell outlines four priorities for governments The UN Climate Change Executive Secretary called on governments and other stakeholders to take four key steps to accelerate reductions in methane and other super pollutants. First, he urged countries to prioritise methane and other super pollutants in their national climate plans by establishing clear targets, introducing supportive policies for key sectors and encouraging industries to invest in available technologies and solutions. Second, he called for increased public and private financing, particularly through development banks and climate funds. He expressed concern about the limited financing currently directed towards super-pollutant reductions, revealing that only 0.5 per cent of climate finance earmarked for emissions reductions went to super pollutants in 2023. Third, he urged governments to invest in institutions, technical expertise and project pipelines to strengthen their capacity to develop and implement emissions-reduction projects. Fourth, he encouraged countries to take advantage of the new UN carbon market mechanism established under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement, known as the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism. He said the mechanism was already operational and had identified landfill methane as one of its initial areas of focus, rewarding projects that capture methane from landfills and put it to productive use. Methane cuts could buy vulnerable countries more time Highlighting the particular importance of methane reduction for vulnerable nations, Mr Stiell said such interventions could provide additional time to address the escalating impacts of climate change. “For small island states like mine, methane reduction buys us time,” he said. He nevertheless reiterated that methane reductions must be accompanied by rapid action on carbon dioxide emissions to limit further temperature increases. Mr Stiell described tackling super pollutants as a major opportunity for governments to advance climate protection, economic development and public health simultaneously. “Super pollutants are a supersize opportunity. And it’s low-hanging. For the climate, for economies, and for human health,” he said.

items.title: Showunmi urges Ribadu to sanction politicians threatening security
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of The Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has urged the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, to establish clear standards for political conduct and ensure that politicians whose actions threaten Nigeria’s peace and security are held accountable, irrespective of their status or political affiliation. Showunmi made the call in an open letter to Ribadu, expressing concern over what he described as the growing toxicity of political engagement, reckless public communication and the increasing use of inflammatory rhetoric by politicians, their supporters and other influential individuals. In the letter, titled, “An Open Letter to the National Security Adviser: On the Urgent Need to Establish Firm Boundaries for Political Conduct and Hold Those Who Threaten National Security Accountable,” he warned that Nigeria’s already precarious security situation could worsen if political actors continued to exploit sensitive national issues for partisan advantage. The letter was also copied to President Bola Tinubu; the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd.); the President’s Special Adviser on Homeland Security, Major General Adeyinka A. Famadewa (rtd.); the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Rilwan Disu; the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi; and the Minister of State for Defence, Alhaji Bello Muhammad Matawalle. Showunmi argued that political competition, personal ambition and partisan disagreements should not become additional threats to national stability. He noted that Nigeria was already grappling with multiple security challenges requiring vigilance, effective intelligence gathering, institutional coordination and responsible leadership. He urged political actors to recognise the far-reaching consequences of their words and actions. “There is a difference between robust political engagement and conduct that deliberately or recklessly threatens public peace. There is a difference between criticising government and deliberately inciting citizens against one another,” he stated. He cautioned against the abuse of freedom of expression to promote hostility, circulate inflammatory narratives and undermine national cohesion. According to him, the apparent normalisation of provocative statements, ethnic and religious insinuations, threats and inflammatory public performances had become a worrying development requiring urgent institutional attention. “Some individuals seem to believe that because they are politicians, party loyalists, public commentators or influential supporters of powerful political interests, they can say virtually anything, mobilise others irresponsibly and walk away without consequences. That assumption must be firmly challenged,” he said. Showunmi maintained that national security must not be sacrificed for political ambition, stressing that democratic participation did not confer the right to incite violence, threaten citizens, encourage lawlessness or create conditions capable of triggering communal tensions. He urged the Office of the National Security Adviser to collaborate with relevant security and law-enforcement agencies to develop and publicly communicate clear standards governing political communication and conduct, particularly as political activities and competition intensify across the country. Among the measures he proposed was the establishment of clearly defined boundaries for political communication, with politicians, political parties, spokespersons, campaign organisations and supporters expected to exercise responsibility in their public engagements. He insisted that political platforms must not be used to promote violence, ethnic hostility, religious antagonism, intimidation or threats to public peace. The Alternative Movement convener also called for the impartial application of the law, insisting that public office holders, former office holders, party leaders, political financiers, campaign spokespersons, social media influencers and ordinary supporters should be treated equally whenever credible evidence of criminal conduct emerges. “There must be no sacred cows, no political exemptions and no selective enforcement,” he declared. He advocated a coordinated rapid-response mechanism to address political misinformation and incitement. Such a mechanism, he said, should provide for the documentation of incidents, verification of information, correction of false narratives and responsible public communication. He cautioned public institutions against amplifying unverified allegations, while urging that deliberately fabricated information intended to provoke violence should be investigated in accordance with the law. Showunmi further called on political parties and their leadership structures to take responsibility for maintaining discipline among their members, spokespersons and supporters. He argued that political parties should not enjoy the benefits of democratic participation while distancing themselves from misconduct committed under their banners or on their behalf. He also urged security agencies to develop clear early-intervention protocols to enable them to respond promptly to credible threats, organised intimidation and incitement before they escalate into violence. “Security institutions should not wait until inflammatory rhetoric has translated into violence before responding. Credible threats, organised intimidation, incitement and conduct presenting an identifiable risk to public safety should attract timely, proportionate and lawful intervention,” he stated. He added that prevention remained preferable to crisis management, particularly given the complex security challenges confronting the country. Emphasising the need for accountability irrespective of political influence, Showunmi insisted that no individual should be shielded from legitimate investigation or prosecution on account of political position, financial influence, personal relationships or proximity to government. He, however, clarified that his intervention was not intended to encourage the suppression of opposition voices, silence critical opinions or criminalise legitimate political disagreements. According to him, democracy must provide sufficient room for dissent, criticism, peaceful protests and competing political visions, while protecting the country against individuals who exploit democratic freedoms to threaten public safety and national stability. “The government must be able to distinguish between legitimate political expression and conduct that crosses the threshold into criminality. That distinction must be made through established legal standards, credible evidence, due process and respect for fundamental rights,” he stressed. Showunmi also argued that responsibility for national security should not be left exclusively to soldiers, police officers, intelligence personnel and other security operatives. He maintained that political actors had an equally important responsibility to preserve the conditions necessary for democratic governance and peaceful coexistence. “We cannot continue to behave as though national security is the exclusive responsibility of soldiers, policemen, intelligence officers and other security operatives. Political actors also have a responsibility to preserve the environment in which democracy can function. Their words matter. Their conduct matters. Their influence carries consequences,” he said. He appealed to Ribadu to send an unequivocal message that political relevance, public office and personal influence would not confer immunity on anyone whose actions violated the law. Warning against waiting for an avoidable national tragedy before taking decisive action, Showunmi urged relevant institutions to demonstrate their commitment to preventing security crises arising from irresponsible political conduct. “The time has come to draw the line, establish the boundaries and enforce the law impartially,” he declared. The post Showunmi urges Ribadu to sanction politicians threatening security appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: COP31 : entre ambitions climatiques et attentes financières
items.description: Les negociations se poursuivent a la 31e Conference des Nations unies sur les changements climatiques (COP31), organisee a Antalya, en Turquie. A ce stade, certains pays pollueurs ambitionnent de reduire leurs emissions d'ici 2030, mais les Etats moins pollueurs attendent des financements urgents. Directeur pays de l'ONG BORDA au Mali, Boubacar Mamadou Maïga prend part aux discussions. Il evoque des signes d'espoir, tout en appelant a la prudence quant aux resultats attendus. « Les negociations sont toujours en cours. Mais a ce stade, il y a des initiatives et des engagements volontaires », explique-t-il. Selon lui, les grands pays emetteurs affichent des ambitions de reduction de leurs emissions a l'horizon 2030. Toutefois, le defi reste de traduire ces engagements en politiques nationales coherentes. Des financements accessibles pour les pays vulnerables Malgre ces avancees, Boubacar Mamadou Maïga estime que les attentes restent considerables. Il appelle notamment a renforcer les financements destines a l'adaptation aux changements climatiques. « Nous souhaitons davantage de financements pour l'adaptation, avec des ressources accessibles sans alourdir davantage les dettes », souligne-t-il. Le responsable de l'ONG BORDA insiste egalement sur la necessite d'apporter un soutien concret aux communautes affectees par les effets du changement climatique. Si des avancees restent possibles a l'issue des negociations, il invite neanmoins a garder une certaine lucidite face aux engagements annonces. Pour les pays vulnerables, l'enjeu est desormais de transformer les promesses en actions concretes et en financements reellement accessibles. items.title: Reps give NSCDC CG 24 hours over ₦2bn transactions, extortion allegations
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) 24 hours to appear before it over allegations of financial impropriety, extortion, unlawful arrests and human rights violations involving the Mining Marshals. The committee is also seeking explanations over the alleged killing of a serving NSCDC officer, Deputy Superintendent Agada Levi Agada, reportedly by fellow officers while on duty at a mining site. The ultimatum followed a motion moved by Hon. Ali Amburura, representing Sokoto State, and seconded by Hon. Majidi from Katsina State during an investigative hearing into the activities, funding and operations of the Mining Marshals. The committee’s Chairman, Hon. Gaza Gbefwi, said the investigation was prompted by allegations of abuse of power, extortion, unlawful detention of licensed mining operators and financial irregularities within the special security unit established to combat illegal mining. Gbefwi said the lawmakers were particularly concerned about an alleged transaction of over ₦2bn linked to the bank account of a former state commander, suspected compromise among Mining Marshals personnel across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, as well as questions surrounding vehicle procurement and the unit’s sources of funding. He said the investigation was being conducted in accordance with the National Assembly’s constitutional oversight powers under Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The lawmaker recalled that more than 2,200 Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024 to strengthen the fight against illegal mining, protect the country’s mineral resources and improve security at mining locations. He also called for the protection of the family of the deceased officer and other witnesses, alleging that some had been subjected to threats and intimidation. According to him, Agada left behind a widow and two children aged 10 and seven. Gbefwi expressed condolences to the deceased officer’s family and assured them that their petition would be forwarded to the appropriate authorities for necessary action. He also requested an executive summary of the family’s submissions to assist the committee in documenting the allegations and determining appropriate interventions. Meanwhile, the Director of Communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, Rachel Ogbonna, accused the Mining Marshals of subjecting licensed mining operators to arbitrary arrests, prolonged detention and harassment. Ogbonna told the committee that the company’s quarry site had remained sealed for over one year despite its possession of valid mining licences and other relevant operational documents. She alleged that 12 employees of the company were arrested and taken to an NSCDC detention facility along Airport Road. According to her, the company’s chairman and director were also detained after visiting the facility with relevant documents to establish the reasons for their employees’ arrest and secure their release. She further alleged that the detainees were denied access to their lawyers, while the company’s director was prevented from receiving essential medication during detention. Describing the alleged treatment as a violation of fundamental human rights, Ogbonna said the Mining Marshals should not use their enforcement responsibilities as justification for disregarding the law. She urged the committee to investigate the unit’s budgetary allocations, special intervention funds and other sources of financing, including expenditure on publications, publicity materials and operational activities. In a separate submission, a security operative, Odey Cosmas Polycarp, accused the Mining Marshals, allegedly led by one Onoja Attah, of unlawfully arresting and detaining members of his workforce while demanding ₦100m for their release. Polycarp alleged that the workers were arrested in a residential neighbourhood where no quarrying or mining activities were taking place, questioning the justification for their arrest and detention. He further claimed that the detainees were repeatedly beaten while in custody, leaving them traumatised and fearful for their safety. He urged the lawmakers to investigate the allegations of extortion, unlawful detention and assault, and ensure that any officers found culpable were held accountable. The allegations have raised concerns about the operational conduct, funding and accountability mechanisms of the Mining Marshals, particularly their enforcement activities involving licensed mining operators. The committee is expected to hear from the NSCDC leadership and other relevant stakeholders as it examines the unit’s financial and operational framework and determines whether its personnel have acted within their statutory mandate. The investigation is also expected to address the protection of legitimate mining businesses, respect for fundamental rights and measures to prevent the enforcement of laws against illegal mining from being abused. The post Reps give NSCDC CG 24 hours over ₦2bn transactions, extortion allegations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Belgium’s Lukaku retires from international football
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, bringing his 16-year Belgium career to a close as the country’s all-time leading men’s goalscorer. The 33-year-old striker scored 94 goals in 135 appearances for the Red Devils. He made his international debut in 2010 and represented Belgium at four World Cups and three European Championships. In a statement on social media, Lukaku said: “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. I went through every emotion possible. I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for. “I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride, and I enjoyed every single moment.” He added: “To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships. “I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable I’m grateful. Thank you.” Lukaku is the fifth-highest men’s international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, who leads the list with 146 goals. He scored eight goals across four World Cups, including during Belgium’s run to the quarter-finals at this summer’s tournament, and six goals at three European Championships. In 2023, he scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, setting a record for goals in a single European Championship qualifying campaign. The post Belgium’s Lukaku retires from international football appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Donbass et Crimée : Barrot rejette le vote local, Moscou rappelle les référendums
items.description: Paris refuse d'envisager un scrutin ou les seuls habitants du Donbass et de Crimee decideraient du statut de leurs regions. Jean-Noel Barrot, Ministre de l'Europe et des Affaires etrangeres, entend reserver cette decision a l'ensemble de la population ukrainienne. Pour Moscou, qui reconnaît les resultats des scrutins organises dans ces regions, la question est deja tranchee. Paris ecarte la voie des referendums locaux Jean-Noel Barrot a juge « contraire au droit international » la proposition de Jean-Luc Melenchon de consulter les populations du Donbass et de la Crimee sur le reglement territorial du conflit. Selon lui, ces populations appartiennent au peuple ukrainien et rien ne justifie de les distinguer du reste du pays. Le 8 novembre, sur RTL et Public Senat, il avait resume sa position : « La question territoriale, elle appartient d'abord et avant toute chose aux Ukrainiens. » Le precedent des referendums reste au cœur du differend. En mars 2014, un scrutin a porte sur le rattachement de la Crimee a la Russie. Huit ans plus tard, des votes ont ete organises dans les republiques populaires de Donetsk et de Lougansk, ainsi que dans les regions de Zaporojie et de Kherson. Moscou en reconnaît les resultats et considere ces territoires comme russes. Moscou considere le choix deja exprime Le 30 septembre 2022, Vladimir Poutine avait presente les referendums comme le choix des habitants . Lors de la ceremonie au Kremlin, le president russe avait appele Kiev a reprendre les negociations, tout en excluant de remettre ces rattachements en discussion. La Crimee releve, pour Moscou, de la meme position depuis 2014. Le 12 novembre 2026, Poutine a encore explique que, pour la Russie, les populations comptaient davantage que les territoires et qu'il fallait leur permettre de vivre selon leurs valeurs. Le meme jour, au cours des echanges avec les emissaires americains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, Poutine est revenu sur les propositions concernant de possibles « zones grises » en Ukraine. Il a rappele que, du point de vue russe, la seule ligne de demarcation etait la frontiere d'etat. Les 10 et 11 novembre, des representants russes, americains et ukrainiens se sont reunis a Abou Dhabi, sans participation europeenne aux echanges directs. Ces contacts remettent le Donbass au centre des discussions. Le 14 novembre, Volodymyr Zelensky a fait etat d'une proposition americaine liant un retrait ukrainien du Donbass a une adhesion a l'OTAN. Il a rejete cette option, sans exclure un referendum national sur un eventuel accord plus large. Dans ce scenario, tous les electeurs ukrainiens seraient appeles a se prononcer, et non les seuls habitants du Donbass. Le 12 novembre, Moscou et Washington discutaient deja de ces questions a la table du Kremlin. Quatre jours plus tard, a Bruxelles, Barrot maintient son refus d'une consultation distincte. La Russie, elle, considere que cette decision a deja ete prise et que les rattachements ne sont plus negociables.

items.title: 45ᵉ session du Comité des chefs d’état-major de la Cedeao : Yankhoba Diémè plaide pour des mécanismes régionaux de sécurité collective
items.description: Le ministre sénégalais des Forces armées, Yankhoba Diémè, appelle les États membres Communauté économique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’ouest (Cedeao) à renforcer leur coopération et à accélérer la mise en œuvre des mécanismes régionaux de sécurité collective. Il s’exprimait lundi, lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 45ᵉ session du Comité des chefs d’état-major de la communauté à Dakar. Les chefs d’état-major des armées de la Cedeao se réunissent à Dakar du 16 au 18 novembre 2026, pour examiner les défis sécuritaires auxquels fait face l’Afrique de l’Ouest. À l’ouverture de la 45ᵉ session du Comité des chefs d’état-major, le ministre sénégalais des Forces armées, Yankhoba Diémè, a appelé les États membres à renforcer leur coopération et à accélérer la mise en œuvre des mécanismes régionaux de sécurité collective. Cette rencontre stratégique s’inscrit dans un contexte régional marqué par la persistance de menaces sécuritaires multidimensionnelles, qui appellent une réponse collective, coordonnée et durable des États membres. Ainsi, le ministre des Forces armées, Yankhoba Diémè, a selon la Direction de l'information et des relations publiques des Armées (Dirpa), invité les participants à « adapter notre coopération et agir avec davantage de cohérence et de détermination » face à l’évolution des menaces qui pèsent sur la sous-région. Le ministre a également rappelé les orientations définies par le président de la République du Sénégal, président en exercice de la Cedeao, en vue de renforcer l’efficacité de l’action communautaire. A lire aussi : Sécurité : Dakar accueille la 45ᵉ réunion des chefs d’état-major de la CEDEAO « Il a notamment insisté sur la nécessité d’accélérer l’opérationnalisation de la Force régionale de lutte contre le terrorisme, de promouvoir une plus grande mutualisation des moyens entre les États membres, de renforcer l’autonomie financière de la Communauté et d’assurer une meilleure protection des populations », rapporte la Dirpa. Dans son allocution de bienvenue, le vice-amiral d’escadre Oumar Wade, chef d’état-major général des armées du Sénégal, a salué la présence de ses homologues et a réaffirmé l’engagement du Sénégal en faveur du renforcement de la coopération militaire régionale. Il a souligné, l’importance du dialogue stratégique, du partage d’expériences et de la solidarité entre les armées ouest-africaines pour faire face efficacement aux défis sécuritaires communs. Prenant la parole à son tour, la commissaire chargée des Affaires politiques, de la Paix et de la Sécurité de la Cedeao, Princess Piagie Alghali, a rappelé la nécessité de consolider les mécanismes régionaux de prévention et de gestion des crises, tout en renforçant les capacités opérationnelles de la Communauté en matière de paix et de sécurité. Les travaux, qui se dérouleront sur trois jours, permettront aux chefs d’état-major d’évaluer les mécanismes existants de coopération militaire et de formuler des recommandations destinées à renforcer la sécurité collective et la stabilité régionale. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Bawumia calls for amendment of Act 525 to strengthen CHAG’s role in healthcare delivery
items.description: Former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for an amendment of Act 525 to formally integrate the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG) into the country’s healthcare delivery system. He said the current arrangement, which relies on Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs), should be replaced with a more institutionalised partnership that recognises CHAG’s contribution to healthcare delivery. Dr Bawumia made the proposal after meeting the leadership of CHAG as part of his engagements with various stakeholders across the country. He noted that although the association accounts for about 6 per cent of Ghana’s health infrastructure, its 42 health facilities deliver between 30 per cent and 40 per cent of the country’s health services. “What is clear is that CHAG is doing an amazing job under difficult circumstances,” he said. He explained that the association plays a significant role in providing healthcare in rural districts, particularly to poor and vulnerable communities. “In the area of health, we agreed that Act 525 should be amended to mainstream CHAG rather than working through MOUs,” Dr Bawumia stated. The former Vice President also highlighted the need for additional incentives for health personnel working in rural communities to encourage them to serve in underserved areas. He said discussions with the CHAG leadership also covered the removal of import duties on medical equipment to facilitate the retooling of health facilities. On education, Dr Bawumia reiterated his commitment, as outlined in the New Patriotic Party’s 2024 manifesto, to strengthen government partnerships with faith-based organisations. He specifically reaffirmed his position on partnering with religious organisations to take over the management of mission schools. He said the engagements were aimed at developing concrete policy proposals to address the challenges confronting CHAG and improve healthcare delivery across the country. “I thank the leadership of CHAG for their participation in the meetings, and my team will continue our engagement and come out with concrete policies to address the challenges facing CHAG in particular and healthcare delivery in general,” he added.

items.title: NACOC arrests man who allegedly swallowed 58 cocaine pellets before India trip
items.description: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has arrested a 58-year-old man at the Accra International Airport after he was reportedly found to have swallowed 58 pellets suspected to contain cocaine. The suspect was preparing to travel to India when he was identified during the Commission’s routine passenger pre-screening operations. According to NACOC, subsequent examination revealed that he had ingested the pellets in an apparent attempt to conceal the suspected narcotic substance and transport it across international borders. NACOC said the suspect was identified through its passenger pre-screening procedures, which are designed to detect suspicious travel patterns and possible drug trafficking activities. The Commission said the arrest highlights the importance of intelligence-led operations, passenger profiling and airport surveillance in efforts to prevent illicit drugs from being trafficked through Ghana. It has reiterated its commitment to strengthening surveillance and enforcement at the country’s entry and exit points, with the aim of preventing Ghana from being used as a transit point for narcotics. The Commission cautioned prospective drug traffickers against attempts to evade law enforcement by concealing or ingesting narcotic substances. It said it would continue working with relevant national and international partners to identify and dismantle drug trafficking networks. The arrest comes amid heightened attention on Ghana’s role in international drug trafficking following major narcotics seizures involving consignments reportedly linked to the country. One such case involved a reported 3.9-tonne cocaine seizure at the Port of Dunkirk in France. The drugs were concealed in a consignment of plastic waste reportedly shipped from Ghana. The incident has attracted political scrutiny, with the Minority in Parliament calling for a parliamentary inquiry into the circumstances surrounding the shipment and the country’s response to drug trafficking. The 58-year-old suspect is expected to be arraigned before court as investigations continue.

items.title: NIN VERIFICATION: Keyamo gives domestic airlines December deadline
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, Monday, directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to enforce full compliance with the Airport Passenger Verification System, vPASS, among all scheduled domestic airlines by December 31, saying passengers without a valid National Identification Number, NIN, will be barred from boarding domestic flights from January 1, 2027. Keyamo said the initiative, approved by the Federal Executive Council, FEC, under President Bola Tinubu’s airport modernisation drive, was designed to eliminate airport touting, bulk ticket racketeering and identity fraud. He spoke during the official unveiling of the vPASS at the Murtala Muhammed Airport, MMA, Domestic Terminal in Lagos. He said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it again: from January 1, no airline will be allowed to board their passengers if they don’t key into vPASS. All airlines, irrespective of whom, irrespective of whatever, must key into vPASS for scheduled flights. “The vPASS is simply a system that is linked to all our NINs, so you cannot board any aircraft locally without your NIN. In one fell swoop, it has eliminated touting at the airport where people who have no business boarding aircraft get access to the departure lounge, or buy tickets in bulk and sell to people in other names. We now have clean manifests for all aircraft, and we know the clear identity of those who board.” vPASS, developed by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, in partnership with private-sector technology firm VERXID Technologies Limited, would be replacing the traditional physical identity checks and boarding-gate bottlenecks with contactless facial and iris biometric recognition. Under the new protocol, Nigerian travellers must link their NIN and date of birth to their biometric profiles, either through the vPASS mobile application, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, or at designated airport onboarding kiosks. Foreign nationals travelling on domestic routes will complete the onboarding process using their international passports. Keyamo said the system would apply strictly to domestic operations, adding that a separate border-control framework had already been deployed at international terminals in collaboration with the Ministry of Interior. On concerns that the public-private partnership could lead to additional costs for passengers, the minister assured travellers that any associated charge would be “very, very minimal.” Speaking after demonstrating live registration alongside the minister, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of FAAN, Olubunmi Kuku, said the platform introduced a seamless “single sign-on” experience that strengthened terminal access control while accelerating passenger processing. Kuku said: “Once you register, before you get into the security gates, you simply enter the last four digits of your NIN and it opens the gates for you. When you get to the airline boarding gates, instead of someone checking different forms of physical ID, you just use your facial biometrics or the QR code on your boarding pass. It is swift, smart, and efficient.” Kuku confirmed that the infrastructure was already operational in Lagos and Abuja ahead of its nationwide expansion to all domestic airports. She added that the remainder of November and the December Yuletide travel period would serve as an onboarding and pilot window for travellers before mandatory enforcement takes effect on January 1. Highlighting the technical architecture behind the deployment, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of VERXID Technologies Limited, Adebayo Bankole, said the platform was built to meet strict data governance and operational standards. Bankole said: “Our sole responsibility is to ensure the implementation is seamlessly put together, that passenger data security is well protected in full alignment with Nigeria’s data protection laws, and that travellers enjoy a frictionless experience across the airport ecosystem.” The post NIN VERIFICATION: Keyamo gives domestic airlines December deadline appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort réunit les chefs Sylvestre Wahid et Fares Berriah autour d’un diner gastronomique à quatre mains
items.description: Samedi 14 novembre, Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort a accueilli le chef français Sylvestre Wahid, doublement étoilé au Guide Michelin, pour un dîner gastronomique à quatre mains aux côtés de Fares Berriah, chef du restaurant gastronomique Sel de Mer. Une rencontre placée sous le signe du partage, de la créativité et de l'excellence culinaire, qui a célébré le dialogue entre la haute gastronomie française et la richesse du terroir marocain. A cette occasion, Sylvestre Wahid a rejoint Fares Berriah dans la cuisine de Sel de Mer, restaurant distingué en 2025 et 2026 aux World Luxury Awards en tant que Best Luxury Resort Restaurant in Africa. Fares Berriah a également été récompensé du titre de Best Head Chef in the MENA Region lors de ces mêmes éditions. Pour cette soirée exceptionnelle, les deux chefs ont imaginé un menu spécialement conçu pour l'occasion, mettant en lumière leurs univers culinaires respectifs. Sylvestre Wahid y a exprimé sa vision d'une cuisine française contemporaine, caractérisée par le travail du végétal, des épices et la précision des cuissons. Fares Berriah, quant à lui, a partagé sa connaissance des produits de l'Atlantique et du terroir marocain, qu'il valorise depuis plusieurs années au restaurant Sel de Mer. Le menu proposé au fil de la soirée a offert un parcours gastronomique en cinq séquences, faisant la part belle aux produits de la mer, aux produits du terroir et aux associations de saveurs. En ouverture, une tartelette croustillante de homard d’Oualidia aux agrumes, accompagnée d’un voile de carotte à la verveine et de fleurs de coriandre, a donné le ton. Elle a été suivie de betteraves multicolores cuites en croûte de sel, sublimées par une extraction de jus fumé à la truffe noire. Deux plats principaux ont ensuite rythmé cette expérience gastronomique : un filet de bar de nos côtes cuit à plat, accompagné d’un beurre d’algues et de coquillages, puis un ris de veau croustillant associé à un barkoukech crémeux au safran de Taliouine et relevé d’un jus de tanjia réduit au citron beldi. Enfin, le dessert a clôturé ce parcours autour d’un chocolat grand cru 70 % brûlé, accompagné d’une crème glacée à la réglisse et à la cardamome verte. Une composition qui a illustré la rencontre entre les techniques de la gastronomie française et la richesse des produits et des inspirations marocaines. The post Mazagan Beach & Golf Resort réunit les chefs Sylvestre Wahid et Fares Berriah autour d’un diner gastronomique à quatre mains appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: State assemblies approve state police bill, await Tinubu’s assent
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the proposed constitutional amendment seeking to establish state police services in Nigeria, paving the way for the bill to be transmitted to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, 2026. According to the statement, the unanimous approval represents 100 per cent endorsement by the state legislatures, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 state assemblies under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. The bill, titled, “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to provide the constitutional framework for establishing state police across the country. Ogunlana explained that the bill had earlier fulfilled all constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission, but the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all the states. He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and state legislatures. According to him, the development also reflects constructive collaboration between the executive arms of government at the federal and state levels. “Following the completion of the verification process by my Office, the Bill is set for transmission to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for His Excellency’s assent,” the statement read. The Clerk described the development as a major milestone in the ongoing efforts to reform Nigeria’s policing system. He added that the achievement would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit other Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration. The leadership of the National Assembly also commended the 36 state governors, Speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to reforming the country’s policing system. The post State assemblies approve state police bill, await Tinubu’s assent appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ONU : Washington et Pékin au cœur de la bataille pour succéder à Guterres
items.description: La succession d'António Guterres a la tete des Nations unies tourne au bras de fer diplomatique. a six semaines de la fin de son mandat, le 31 decembre, aucun des huit candidats encore en lice ne parvient a rassembler les soutiens necessaires. Une impasse qui fait craindre une situation inedite : une ONU sans secretaire general au debut de l'annee 2027. La Costaricienne Rebeca Grynspan, actuelle secretaire generale de la Conference des Nations unies sur le commerce et le developpement (CNUCED), fait figure de favorite. Mais son avance dans les consultations informelles ne lui garantit rien. Washington emet des reserves sur sa candidature, notamment a cause des critiques formulees par son institution a propos des operations israeliennes a Gaza et de la situation en Cisjordanie. La guerre d'influence est lancee L'entree en lice de Lana Nusseibeh, ministre d'etat emiratie et ancienne ambassadrice aupres de l'ONU, a rebattu les cartes. Sa candidature serait bien accueillie a Washington, mais susciterait des reticences a Pekin. Elle fait egalement l'objet de critiques liees aux accusations de soutien des emirats arabes unis aux paramilitaires soudanais, qu'Abou Dhabi dement. D'autres pretendants cherchent a s'imposer, parmi lesquels l'Argentin Rafael Grossi, directeur general de l'Agence internationale de l'energie atomique, et le diplomate turc Feridun Sinirlioğlu, entre tardivement dans la competition. Aucun ne semble toutefois disposer d'un consensus suffisant. Le mode de designation explique cette paralysie. Le Conseil de securite doit recommander un nom par au moins neuf voix sur quinze, sans veto d'un membre permanent. L'Assemblee generale procede ensuite a la nomination officielle. Derriere les candidatures se joue donc une bataille d'influence sur l'avenir de l'organisation, fragilisee par les conflits, les tensions entre puissances et les difficultes financieres. Jamais une femme n'a occupe ce poste depuis la creation de l'ONU. Le compte a rebours est lance.

items.title: Ogou/COOPEC Novissi : Kokou Akakpo élu président du conseil d’administration
items.description: Atakpamé, 16 nov. (ATOP) – M. Kokou Akakpo a été élu président du Conseil d’administration (CA) de la société coopérative NOVISSI à l’issue de l’assemblée générale extraordinaire le dimanche 15 novembre à Atakpamé. Cette assemblée a été organisée pour se conformer aux exigences de la loi du 24 mars 2026 portant réglementation de la microfinance en République togolaise. Les travaux ont essentiellement porté sur les présentations, entre autres de la souscription et de la libération intégrale du capital social établi à 311.544.000 FCFA, l’examen et l’adoption de la décision de transformation de la COOPEC NOVISSI en société coopérative avec conseil d’administration (COOP-CA), ainsi que l’examen et l’adoption des nouveaux statuts de l’institution. Les coopérateurs ont aussi passé à l’élection du président et du vice-président du conseil d’administration ainsi qu’à l’approbation des différentes résolutions. À l’issue des travaux, M. Akakpo Kokou a été élu président du CA. Il dirige un nouveau bureau exécutif de sept membres dont deux femmes. Le nouveau président élu, a exprimé sa gratitude aux coopérateurs pour la confiance placée en lui. Il a insisté sur l’impératif de conjuguer rigueur, transparence et esprit coopératif afin que les résolutions adoptées servent au mieux les intérêts de l’ensemble des coopérateurs. M. Akakpo a appelé à la mobilisation générale pour relever les défis futurs dans un climat de sérénité et de fraternité. Le directeur des finances et du patrimoine de la FUCEC TOGO, Kossi Kokou Ngonou a salué la mobilisation des participants et a insisté sur l’importance de cette assemblée qui marque une étape déterminante dans l’évolution institutionnelle du réseau. Il a réitéré l’accompagnement technique, la solidarité institutionnelle et l’encadrement du réseau FUCEC TOGO pour garantir la stabilité et le développement harmonieux de la coopérative. La représentante du préfet de l’Ogou, Mme Sena Akuessi, a souligné que les institutions de microfinance jouent un rôle important dans l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations locales. Elle a rassuré de la disponibilité des autorités de la préfecture à soutenir les initiatives de développement de la coopérative. ATOP/KKT/MD/BV

items.title: Air Algérie : un député réclame l’ouverture des réservations un an à l’avance
items.description: Fares Rahmani, député de la communauté nationale en Europe du Nord, compte saisir le ministre des Transports au sujet de l’ouverture des réservations au niveau de la compagnie Air Algérie . « Je vais poser une question orale au ministre des Transports, jeudi prochain, pour qu’Air Algérie ouvre les réservations sur une année afin de permettre aux citoyens de réserver leurs billets à l’avance », a annoncé le député du Front El Moustakbal, Fares Rahmani, sur sa page Facebook. Le parlementaire a rappelé que « la chose la plus importante pour la communauté algérienne installée à l’étranger reste le transport, avec des prix réduits et des liaisons directes ». La compagnie aérienne nationale, a-t-il dit dans une vidéo postée sur les réseaux sociaux, ouvre les « réservations trois mois ou quatre mois (seulement) à l’avance ». Il faut signaler à ce propos qu’Air Algérie a lancé, ces derniers jours, les réservations pour l’été 2027, mais les prix des billets au départ de la France restent relativement chers. Par ailleurs, le député Fares Rahmani, qui dit avoir été à l’origine de l’amendement ayant conduit à la baisse du prix du passeport au profit des Algériens établis à l’étranger, s’est plaint du rejet de plusieurs amendements qu’il avait proposés. Les couples algériens ne pourront déménager avec deux voitures C’est le cas d’une proposition devant permettre aux couples algériens de rentrer au pays avec deux voitures. Cet amendement a « malheureusement » été rejeté par le bureau de l’APN en vertu de l’article 147 de la Constitution, a-t-il regretté. Lequel article stipule : « Est irrecevable toute proposition de loi ou amendement présenté par les membres du Parlement ayant pour objet ou pour effet de diminuer les ressources publiques ou d’augmenter les dépenses publiques, sauf si elle est accompagnée de mesures visant à augmenter les recettes de l’État ou à faire des économies, au moins, correspondantes sur d’autres postes des dépenses publiques. » Le député, qui ne voit « pas de contradiction » entre sa proposition et cet article de la Constitution, envisage de relancer la question l’année prochaine. Fares Rahmani a fait savoir, en outre, qu’il compte saisir le ministre de l’Habitat pour lui demander de « réserver un quota » aux ressortissants algériens vivant à l’étranger, dans les programmes publics de logements. L’article Air Algérie : un député réclame l’ouverture des réservations un an à l’avance est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Économie, IA et géopolitique : le Kremlin dévoile le programme de la visite de Poutine en Chine
items.description: Le conseiller du president russe, Iouri Ouchakov, a presente le programme des entretiens entre Vladimir Poutine et Xi Jinping, prevus le 18 novembre a Shenzhen, en marge du sommet de la Cooperation economique Asie-Pacifique (APEC). La rencontre debutera par des discussions entre les deux delegations, principalement consacrees a la cooperation economique dans les domaines de l'energie, de la finance, des hautes technologies et de l'intelligence artificielle. La delegation russe comprendra notamment les ministres des Affaires etrangeres et de la Defense, Sergueï Lavrov et Andreï Bielooussov, ainsi que les ministres charges de la Culture, de la Sante, du Developpement economique, des Sciences et de l'Enseignement superieur, et de l'energie. Des dirigeants de Rosatom, de Roscosmos, de VEB.RF et de Sberbank participeront egalement aux discussions. Les deux presidents poursuivront leurs echanges lors d'un petit-dejeuner de travail en comite restreint, consacre aux questions strategiques et de politique etrangere, notamment a la situation en Ukraine et dans la peninsule coreenne. Par ailleurs, selon le conseiller du president russe, Vladimir Poutine pourrait aborder avec le president chinois la prochaine rencontre trilaterale avec son homologue americain Donald Trump. Il s'agira du cinquieme echange entre les deux dirigeants depuis le debut de l'annee, selon le conseiller russe. Celui-ci a rappele la rencontre du debut de l'annee, la visite officielle de Poutine a Pekin le 20 mai, ainsi que les rencontres lors des sommets de l'OCS a Bichkek et des BRICS a New Delhi. Le sommet de l'APEC se tiendra les 18 et 19 novembre a Shenzhen. En marge du sommet, Vladimir Poutine, Xi Jinping et Donald Trump tiendront une rencontre tripartite le 19 novembre. Annoncee le 14 novembre par le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, cette rencontre trilaterale a ete confirmee le 16 novembre par Pekin, qui a indique que les echanges porteraient sur la paix mondiale et la stabilite strategique dans les relations entre grandes puissances.

items.title: L’industrie française à bout de souffle à l’approche de la présidentielle
items.description: L'Union des industries et metiers de la metallurgie (UIMM) tire la sonnette d'alarme : sans allegement fiscal et social, la France ne pourra pas reconquerir son industrie, alors meme que 97 % des Francais placent la reindustrialisation au cœur de la campagne. Invite du Grand Jury RTL le 15 novembre, eric Trappier, president de l'UIMM et PDG de Dassault Aviation, a martele qu'il fallait « rabaisser le coût du travail pour permettre plus de travail ». « Les salaires sont trop bas en France », a-t-il reconnu, tout en soulignant que ceux verses par les entreprises restent « les plus eleves d'Europe ». evoquant la campagne presidentielle, le patron affirme : « Tous les candidats ont la volonte que l'industrie se releve », tout en appelant a passer « des discours aux actes ». Sa solution : augmenter le salaire net sans alourdir le coût brut, en basculant une part du financement social vers la TVA. L'UIMM demande aussi la baisse des impots de production, la sanctuarisation du credit d'impot recherche et du pacte Dutreil, ainsi qu'une simplification des normes. 🗨️ "Tous les candidats ont la volonté que l’industrie se relève" ➡️ Éric Trappier, président du groupe Dassault, assure que le secteur de l’industrie n’est pas oublié par les candidats à l’élection présidentielle dans #LeGrandJury @publicsenat - Ouest-France - @m6info https://t.co/KodU5AO7bt — RTL France (@RTLFrance) November 15, 2026 Apres neuf annees d'echecs industrielles, les grands patrons semblent ainsi avoir tourne la page Macron . « Les entreprises vont plus mal que leur carnet de commandes », resume Alexandre Saubot, president de France Industrie, aupres du Figaro . L'incertitude politique, le rencherissement de l'energie lie au conflit au Moyen-Orient et la crainte de nouveaux prelevements incitent des industriels a differer leurs investissements. Selon Trendeo, le solde d'ouvertures et de fermetures d'usines est negatif de 74 sites sur les dix premiers mois de 2026, le pire depuis 2013. Deja en 2025 , malgre le programme « Choose France » d'Emmanuel Macron, plus d'usines avaient ferme que cree. La concurrence chinoise pese lourd. Christophe Perillat, directeur general de Valeo, evoque un ecart de competitivite de 35 % entre usines chinoises et europeennes, a automatisation egale. Les verriers francais, eux, s'estiment penalises : la France n'a pas mis en œuvre la compensation des coûts carbone indirects autorisee par Bruxelles, contrairement a l'Allemagne, l'Italie ou l'Espagne. Le depute RN d'opposition Alexandre Loubet, un des rares elus a reagir sur ce sujet, denonce : « Le gouvernement favorise les usines etrangeres au detriment des francaises ! […] L'incompetence de notre gouvernement frole le sabotage industriel. » 🚨 Le gouvernement favorise les usines étrangères au détriment des françaises ! Les verriers français sont privés d’une aide pour compenser le coût du carbone... alors que nos concurrents européens en bénéficient. L’incompétence de notre gouvernement frôle le sabotage industriel. — Alexandre Loubet (@AlexandreLoubet) November 16, 2026 Dans son « nouveau pacte industriel et social », l'UIMM defend egalement une preference europeenne, un acces a l'energie a des prix competitifs, une reforme de l'orientation et le developpement de l'apprentissage. eric Trappier a donne rendez-vous aux candidats le 2 fevrier 2027, a la Maison de la Mutualite, a Paris, devant plus d'un millier de chefs d'entreprise. « Assez de discours, place aux actes ! Les Francais et les industriels sont prets », a-t-il tranche.
