items.title: CAN 2027 – Soudan-Sénégal (2-4) : Pathé Mboup, la magie opère encore !
items.description: Le Sénégal a fait un grand pas vers la qualification à la CAN 2027. En déplacement à Juba, les Lions ont dominé le Soudan (4-2), au terme d'une rencontre spectaculaire. Après avoir parfaitement maîtrisé la première période, les hommes de Patrick Vieira ont perdu le contrôle au retour des vestiaires, avant de retrouver leur efficacité grâce à un Pathé Mboup encore décisif. Avec cette victoire, les champions d’Afrique confortent leur première place dans le groupe J et se rapprochent de la qualification. Lire aussi: Sénégal-Soudan (4-1) : de la magie dans l’air au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor Les Lions ont pourtant démarré la rencontre pied au plancher. Dès la 4e minute, Nicolas Jackson a montré la voie en ouvrant le score. Dominateur, le Sénégal a rapidement pris le jeu à son compte et Malick Diouf a doublé la mise à la 22e minute. Les Sénégalais semblaient alors avoir la rencontre bien en main. Mais Jackson a manqué une belle occasion d'inscrire le troisième but avant la pause. Un raté qui allait laisser les Soudanais en vie. Lire aussi: De « Magic in the Air » à la Tanière : le joli destin de Pathé Mboup Car au retour des vestiaires, le visage du Sénégal a changé. Moins entreprenants, les Lions ont laissé leurs adversaires reprendre confiance dans cette chaleur de Juba. Nooh a réduit le score à la 52e minute, avant que Hassan ne remette les deux équipes à égalité à la 75e minute. En quelques minutes, l'avance sénégalaise avait fondu. Le doute s'installait et les Crocodiles du Nil se prenaient à rêver d'un exploit. Le Sénégal sera bien à la CAN Sur son banc, Patrick Vieira a alors décidé de réagir en lançant Dion Lopy, Paul Mendy et Pathé Mboup. Un choix qui allait changer le cours de la rencontre. Comme lors de la précédente sortie des Lions, l'attaquant brestois a fait parler son sens du but. Lancé en profondeur, il a ajusté le gardien soudanais d'un lob plein de finesse pour redonner l'avantage au Sénégal. La magie Mboup ne s'est pas arrêtée là. Dans la foulée, le jeune attaquant s'est mué en passeur pour servir Paul Mendy, auteur du quatrième but sénégalais. Il aurait même pu s'offrir un doublé, mais sa frappe a terminé sur le montant de Mustafa, le géant portier soudanais. Bousculé après la pause, le Sénégal a finalement su remettre les choses en ordre pour repartir de Juba avec les trois points. Pathé Mboup, déjà buteur lors de sa précédente sélection, confirme ainsi ses débuts prometteurs avec les Lions : deux buts en deux apparitions. Cette victoire consolide la première place du Sénégal dans le groupe J. Une victoire du Mozambique face à l'Éthiopie ce mardi permettrait aux Lions de valider officiellement leur qualification pour la CAN 2027, prévue au Kenya, en Ouganda et en Tanzanie. Avec deux dernières rencontres à disputer à domicile, contre l'Éthiopie et le Mozambique, le Sénégal est désormais tout proche de retrouver le grand rendez-vous du football africain. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: Guerre Russie-Ukraine : quelle paix réaliste ?
items.description: Pourquoi l’Europe soutient-elle l’Ukraine ? Au-delà de la solidarité avec Kiev, c’est la défense de l’ordre international et du principe de souveraineté des États qui est en jeu, face à une invasion russe qui les remet directement en cause. Mais jusqu’où ce soutien doit-il aller ? Si le droit international est du côté de l’Ukraine, le rapport de force militaire et démographique lui est défavorable. Dans ces conditions, la reconquête de tous les territoires perdus depuis 2014 apparaît de plus en plus incertaine. L’Europe doit donc éviter de confondre solidarité et soutien inconditionnel. Elle doit clarifier ses objectifs, définir les limites de son engagement et réfléchir aux conditions d’une issue politique. Cette perspective suppose aussi de ne pas négliger l’opinion publique russe, qui pourrait jouer un rôle dans la fin du conflit, comme elle a pu le faire avec la guerre en Afghanistan à l’époque soviétique. Comment concilier défense de la souveraineté ukrainienne, réalisme stratégique et recherche d’une issue à la guerre ? Et quel rôle l’Europe doit-elle jouer dans des négociations avec Moscou ? Mon analyse dans cette vidéo. L’article Guerre Russie-Ukraine : quelle paix réaliste ? est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Amou : Le chef du canton d’Ouma Oluke Agouma III confirmé dans ses fonctions
items.description: Amlamé, 16 nov. (ATOP) – Le décret entérinant la désignation coutumière de Olukè Bertin Nayo Agouma III en qualité de chef du canton de Ouma, dans la commune Amou 1 lui a été remis le samedi 14 novembre à Amlamé. Cet évènement a été rythmé par des rites d’intronisation ancestraux, les prestations d’allégeance des chefs de villages envers le nouveau dépositaire des us et coutumes, la sortie officielle du récipiendaire, la remise de décret et des couleurs nationales. Le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Général de Brigade Dadja Maganawé, a invité le nouveau chef à imprimer à son commandement une marque d’écoute, de rassemblement et d’abnégation. Il a insisté sur la place stratégique qu’occupe l’autorité traditionnelle, tout en lui rappelant son rôle dans la préservation de la paix, l’affermissement de la cohésion sociale et l’impulsion du développement local. Le gouverneur a demandé aux populations de soutenir sans réserve leur nouveau chef, tout en privilégiant le dialogue et la voie pacifique pour le règlement des différends. « La collaboration entre les autorités traditionnelles, administratives et locales demeure essentielle pour répondre aux préoccupations des populations », a-t-il souligné. Le nouveau chef de canton a témoigné sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour la confiance placée en sa personne. Il a pris l’engagement d’œuvrer comme un dirigeant intègre, résolument à l’écoute de l’ensemble de ses administrés, par-delà les sensibilités politiques, religieuses ou les origines sociologiques. Olukè Agouma III a invité ses administrés à transcender les divergences, à placer l’intérêt général au premier plan et à s’investir activement pour faire de Ouma, un canton prospère et apaisé. « Aucun développement durable ne peut se réaliser sans la participation et l’engagement de toutes les composantes de la communauté. Je souhaite que cette reconnaissance constitue le socle d’un nouveau départ marqué par le dialogue, le pardon et la réconciliation», a-t-il déclaré. ATOP/AY/KKT/BA

items.title: Ancelotti admet devoir faire "plus d'efforts" sur le banc du Brésil
items.description: Le sélectionneur du Brésil, l'Italien Carlo Ancelotti, a reconnu lundi que ses performances sur le banc des quintuples champions du monde n'étaient « pas suffisantes » et qu'il devait faire « plus d'efforts » pour améliorer le jeu de la Seleçao, battue samedi par le Japon (3-2). Lors de la conférence de presse avant le match amical mardi à Singapour contre la sélection locale (11h00 françaises), Ancelotti a admis ses faiblesses, notamment sur son bilan en tant que sélectionneur depuis juin 2025 (12 victoires, 4 nuls et 5 défaites). « C'est un nouveau projet, j'aime beaucoup ce que nous faisons mais mon opinion est que ce n'est pas suffisant », a-t-il déclaré. « Je dois faire plus d'efforts pour que la sélection redevienne compétitive. Cela fait longtemps que nous ne le sommes plus », a affirmé l'Italien de 67 ans. La défaite contre le Japon lui a valu de vives critiques au Brésil, notamment de l'ancien joueur Romario, qui a demandé son départ immédiat. « C'est la liberté d'expression et, dans un pays démocratique, tout le monde peut donner son opinion. Romario a donné la sienne et c'est un droit que tout le monde a, que ce soit pour dire des mensonges, des vérités ou des bêtises. La vérité, c'est que Romario parle beaucoup et il en a le droit », a-t-il réagi. Exclu lors du match contre le Japon, Ancelotti sera remplacé sur le banc contre Singapour par l'un de ses adjoints, Francesco Mauri. Le sélectionneur a annoncé « certains changements » dans son onze de départ, notamment dans le secteur défensif qui montre des faiblesses récurrentes (21 buts encaissés en 21 matches). Le trio d'attaquants sera composé d'Estevao, Endrick et Vinicius Jr. The post Ancelotti admet devoir faire "plus d'efforts" sur le banc du Brésil appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘I could lose my life’: Ghanaian gay man held in Swedish detention as asylum case stalls
items.description: A 33-year-old Ghanaian man seeking asylum in Sweden because of his sexuality says he fears for his life if he is returned to Ghana, where he claims he could face imprisonment and brutal attacks for being gay. Samuel Asiamah, whose asylum application remains unresolved, has been held at a detention facility in Åstorp, about an hour north of Malmö, for six months, according to a report by The Irish Times published on September 12, 2026. Despite having valid asylum papers, Asiamah was detained after running away from an asylum camp. His lawyer has reportedly been unable to obtain answers from Swedish authorities about why he continues to be held. The Ghanaian, who fled the country in November 2024, told The Irish Times that he would not cooperate with efforts by Swedish authorities to arrange his return to Ghana because of what he believes awaits him if he is sent back. “There is a difference between co-operation and placing your life in jeopardy,” he said. “If people in prison know you are homosexual, you will be brutalised and assaulted, and you could lose your life.” His case has drawn attention to the difficulties facing asylum seekers as Sweden tightens its migration and refugee policies, despite its longstanding reputation as a country that offers protection to people fleeing persecution. From family rejection to physical attacks Asiamah told The Irish Times that his difficulties in Ghana began within his family after his mother became suspicious of his sexuality. He was raised by his grandmother in the countryside before moving to Accra at the age of 18 to live with his mother, who, according to him, was deeply troubled by the possibility that he was gay. He said she took him to regular church blessing services, hoping to address what she considered a source of shame to the family. “She was upset, then furious and gradually started to neglect me, making comments about me being a shame to her and the family,” he recounted. His home became a place of persistent conflict, prompting him to leave at 19. He subsequently found support through a local LGBTQ+ group called Solace. However, he said his relationship with his first boyfriend exposed him to further hostility, with verbal insults escalating into repeated physical attacks. He still carries a scar from one of the assaults, the report said. Asiamah later met a man identified as “Brother Kofi”, who promised to help him travel to Europe. He reportedly took 60,000 Ghana cedis from his mother’s savings to finance the journey. He was flown through Mauritius to France before travelling to Sweden, where he arrived in November 2024. The man who facilitated the journey allegedly abandoned him. After spending a week homeless, he was offered accommodation by a woman who later asked him to leave when she discovered his sexuality. He told the newspaper that he eventually sought help from Swedish police after they found him on the street one snowy day. Asylum application in limbo Asiamah applied for asylum in Malmö in February 2026, hoping Sweden would provide protection from the hostility he says he experienced in Ghana. But his application has since become a source of uncertainty. According to The Irish Times, he told his case officer in May that Ghana’s Parliament had passed a Bill seeking to criminalise the promotion of LGBTQ+ activities, with proposed prison sentences of up to 10 years. He also referred to a provision that would require friends and family members to report one another. The case officer reportedly dismissed the development as irrelevant to his application because Asiamah had not personally experienced the proposed legal regime. The newspaper reported that the Ghanaian’s concerns about returning home are compounded by the prospect of imprisonment and the risk of abuse if his sexuality becomes known while in custody. Swedish authorities have asked him to contact the Ghanaian Embassy to facilitate his return, but he has refused. Neither the Swedish Migration Agency nor the country’s Migration Ministry responded to The Irish Times when approached for comment on his detention. Sweden’s tougher migration policy Asiamah’s predicament comes against the backdrop of a significant shift in Sweden’s approach to asylum and immigration. The country, once regarded as a leading destination for people fleeing persecution, has tightened its migration policies in recent years, with the issue becoming a major subject of political debate. The Irish Times reported that asylum applications in Sweden had fallen by 96 per cent from their 2015 peak to 6,737 in 2025. The country’s asylum approval rate stood at about 23 per cent, less than half the European Union average, according to the report. The Swedish government has also increased financial incentives for migrants willing to leave the country, raising so-called resettlement grants to 350,000 Swedish kronor, equivalent to about €31,371, for adults prepared to return. The policy shift has raised concerns among asylum support groups and human rights advocates about the treatment of people who say they are fleeing unsafe conditions. An organiser of a Malmö-based asylum support group assisting Asiamah told The Irish Times that Sweden’s approach to vulnerable migrants had changed. “It used to be seen as a victory in Sweden to protect people here from unsafe situations, but these people have been so dehumanised now that getting rid of them quickly is the new victory,” the organiser said. Fear of being sent back The uncertainty surrounding his asylum application and detention has taken a toll on Asiamah’s mental wellbeing. He told the newspaper that he shares a room with two other detainees, has fixed meal times and limited opportunities to spend time outdoors. He also said some inmates were violent criminals. The hardest part, he said, was not knowing what would happen to him. “Sometimes I feel very empty. I used to cry a lot,” he said, adding that he had previously experienced suicidal thoughts. His fears have also been heightened by discussions among European countries about establishing so-called “return hubs” outside the European Union for people whose asylum applications have been unsuccessful. The Irish Times reported that Nigeria and Uganda were among countries being considered as possible host locations. Both countries have the death penalty for people found guilty of criminalised same-sex activity, the newspaper noted. Asiamah said he was alarmed by the discussions, arguing that people genuinely seeking protection could be placed at risk if they were treated like criminals. “They are mixing up people who really need help from the authorities and safety, from bad people, religious extremists and Islamist gangs,” he said. For Asiamah, the prospect of being returned to Ghana remains particularly frightening. He told the newspaper that he sometimes thinks about his former boyfriend, who also left Ghana and is now in Canada. “They let him stay,” he said. His own future, however, remains uncertain as he waits in detention for a decision on his asylum application.

items.title: Asiedu Nketia rejects personality cult politics, says he does not endorse ‘friends’ groups
items.description: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says he does not encourage the formation of groups named after him, insisting that he will not promote personality-based politics within the party. In an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse , Mr Asiedu Nketia said he had discouraged young people from forming groups such as “Friends of Asiedu Nketia”, arguing that such associations could create divisions within the party. “Many youth across the country come together and say they are forming a group for Asiedu Nketia. I say if I select you alone to make you my friends, then what about the rest in the party? So I don’t encourage that,” he said. The outgoing chairman said he was not surprised that some candidates contesting positions in the party’s internal elections were invoking his name and claiming close personal ties to him to strengthen their campaigns. “I’m not surprised that the reports I’m having is that many people who want to win elections go around and say, ‘Oh, I am the boy of Asiedu Nketia. I am the daughter of Asiedu Nketia. I cut his hair. I polish his shoe,’” he said. He also referred to claims by some candidates that he had provided them with vehicles for their campaigns. Mr Asiedu Nketia said he found it interesting that rival candidates sometimes responded to such claims by making their own assertions about their closeness to him. Mr Asiedu Nketia said he would not intervene in the contest or endorse any candidate based on claims of personal association with him. “If you think that using my name is what will help you win your election, you can go ahead. I’m not offended, and I’m not selecting anybody. I’m keeping myself out so that after the election, there will be losers and winners,” he said. He has served as NDC National Chairman since 2022 but has announced that he will not seek re-election. The party is scheduled to hold its National Congress on December 19, 2026, to elect new national officers and choose his successor.

items.title: CNAMGS : l’urgence d’un sauvetage face à une crise qui menace la protection sociale
items.description: Confrontée à de lourds déséquilibres financiers, à des défaillances de gouvernance et à une dette importante envers les prestataires de santé, la Caisse nationale d’assurance maladie et de garantie sociale (CNAMGS) fait l’objet d’un plan de redressement. Réuni ce lundi 16 novembre 2026 à Libreville, sous la présidence du vice-président du gouvernement, Hermann Immongault, le comité de pilotage de la Task Force interministérielle a examiné 23 propositions d’arbitrage destinées à remettre l’organisme sur les rails. Etranglée par ses dettes et ses dysfonctionnements, la CNAMGS sous un ciel orageux. © GabonReview La CNAMGS au bord de l’asphyxie. Lancée le 6 juillet dernier, la Task Force interministérielle chargée de son redressement a livré ses premières conclusions après quatre mois de travaux. Le diagnostic est préoccupant : fragilité financière, insuffisances de gouvernance et de contrôle, contraintes juridiques et institutionnelles. Autant de dysfonctionnements qui pèsent directement sur la qualité des prestations offertes aux assurés. Présidant la séance de travail, Hermann Immongault a rappelé que cette structure n’avait pas vocation à devenir un cadre supplémentaire de concertation. « C’est un outil qui a été mis en place pour apporter des réponses concrètes qui vont être prises au plus haut niveau de l’État sur la question de la CNAMGS » , a-t-il insisté, regrettant au passage le retard enregistré et les absences répétées de certains acteurs, notamment la Fédération des entreprises du Gabon (FEG). Une gouvernance et des finances à reconstruire Parmi les huit enjeux identifiés, quatre sont considérés comme critiques. La gouvernance figure en tête, avec la nécessité de recentrer les missions de la Caisse sur l’assurance maladie et de transférer la gestion des filets sociaux au ministère des Affaires sociales. L’harmonisation des textes relatifs aux Gabonais économiquement faibles (GEF) constitue également un chantier prioritaire. Sur le plan financier, la dette accumulée auprès des prestataires de santé, notamment au titre des évacuations sanitaires, fragilise davantage le dispositif. La sécurisation des ressources passe notamment par le reversement régulier et mensualisé de la Contribution spéciale de solidarité (CSS). Pour la ministre des Affaires sociales, Raïssa Nana Ghogho, cette rencontre devait permettre de trier les propositions et de fixer un calendrier d’exécution. L’objectif, a-t-elle expliqué, est de trouver des solutions pour sortir la CNAMGS du « marasme qui est connu » . Vingt-trois arbitrages attendus Les pistes retenues s’inscrivent dans trois horizons. À court terme, il s’agit de restaurer la trésorerie et de garantir la continuité des soins. À moyen terme, la modernisation de la gouvernance et l’accélération du Registre social unique sont privilégiées. À plus longue échéance, la Task Force envisage de diversifier les ressources, notamment par une fiscalité comportementale et une contribution santé-environnement fondée sur le principe pollueur-payeur. Au total, 23 arbitrages sont attendus pour traduire ces orientations en mesures opérationnelles. Les équipes ont été appelées à accélérer leurs travaux. Pour l’État, l’enjeu dépasse le seul redressement d’un organisme : il s’agit de restaurer la confiance des assurés et de préserver un mécanisme essentiel de solidarité nationale. L’article CNAMGS : l’urgence d’un sauvetage face à une crise qui menace la protection sociale est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Lutte contre l’insalubrité à Sédhiou : deux importantes décharges sauvages éliminées dans le quartier de Moricounda
items.description: Face à l'insalubrité qui gangrène le quartier de Moricounda, Ndoumbé Gaye Sow, volontaire de l'organisation Déclic, a mobilisé les jeunes ce week-end pour éliminer deux importants dépotoirs d'ordures sauvages. Cette initiative portée par le projet « Yaakaari jeunesse et citoyenneté », entend œuvrer pour un environnement sain. Sédhiou – Le quartier de Moricounda 1 a subi ce week-end, une profonde transformation, asphyxiée par des dépotoirs d'ordures sauvages, les jeunes se sont mobilisés pour éradiquer ces déchets dans le cadre du projet Yaakaari jeunesse citoyenneté, initié par le consortium jeunesse Sénégal. Cette initiative, qui est mise en œuvre par Déclic dans les régions de Ziguinchor et de Sédhiou, s'inscrit dans cette dynamique d'engagement des jeunes volontaires. Deux sites ont été évacués, le premier, situés derrière le camp de l’escadron d’intervention et de surveillance de la Gendarmerie de Sédhiou, le second en face de la mosquée de Moricounda. »L’aménagement de ces deux sites constitue une avancée importante dans notre lutte contre l’insalubrité. Cette belle mobilisation démontre que, lorsque nous unissons nos efforts, nous pouvons apporter des changements positifs dans nos communautés », a magnifié Ndoumbé Gaye Sow, volontaire à Déclic et à « Yaakaari jeunesse et Citoyenneté », par ailleurs responsable du projet lutte contre les dépôts sauvages des ordures ménagères. A lire aussi : Lancement du projet Baluo Banko pour la promotion de la culture du manioc Cette initiative vise à lutter contre les dépôts sauvages d’ordures ménagères. « Elle contribue à l’amélioration du cadre de vie des populations » a ajouté Mme Konté, saluant la forte mobilisation communautaire. » l'engagement citoyen est une réalité dans notre contrée, a réagi Amadou Leye Konté, leader communautaire, « c'est pourquoi nous ne ménageons aucun effort pour prendre part aux initiatives de ce genre », a -t-il déclaré. Dans le quartier de Moricounda, l'étroitesse des rues rend difficile la collecte des ordures. « C'est dans ce sens que je sollicite la mairie tout comme la Sonaged de nous mettre des gares de dépôt », a lancé Matar Diédhiou, président du conseil consultatif des jeunes de Sédhiou. D'autres activités sont prévues à la suite de ce week-end d'investissement humain, car on ne peut pas lutter contre ces ordures, estime Mamadou Diédhiou, point focal Déclic, sans valoriser ces espaces. « Nous saluons la présence massive des jeunes et des femme, des écoles sont aussi ciblées pour accélérer la lutte contre l'insalubrité ». Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (correspondant)

items.title: BoG flags renewed inflationary pressures as rate rises to 5.5% in October
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is closely monitoring emerging inflationary pressures following an increase in headline inflation to 5.5% in October 2026, from 5.2% in September. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the latest increase requires a closer examination to determine whether the movement reflects temporary price adjustments or a more persistent shift in underlying inflation trends. Speaking at the opening of the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, the Governor said although inflation remains in single digits and below the Bank’s medium-term target band, the central bank cannot afford to be complacent. He said the committee would examine the contributions of food, non-food and services inflation, alongside developments in inflation expectations. The assessment will also consider the potential impact of movements in fuel prices, transport fares and administered prices on the inflation outlook. “While inflation remains below our medium-term target band, the recent uptick warrants careful examination,” Dr Asiama said. The Governor noted that the committee would use the meeting to take stock of macroeconomic developments throughout 2026 and assess the effectiveness of measures implemented by the central bank. He said the MPC would also determine whether further adjustments to its policy instruments are necessary to preserve the gains made in restoring price stability. The 133rd MPC meeting is the Bank’s final monetary policy meeting for 2026, with its outcome expected to provide direction on monetary policy heading into 2027.

items.title: NDC retained more than 85% of branch executives after 2024 victory – Asiedu Nketia
items.description: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says the party retained more than 85 per cent of its branch executives in its recent internal elections. He described the outcome as a recognition of the grassroots officers who, in his view, contributed to the party’s victory in the 2024 general election. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse , Mr Asiedu Nketia said the retention of the branch executives showed that the party had acknowledged their work. “What makes me happier is that in the branch elections that we just conducted, we retained more than 85% of the branch executives who contributed to getting us this unprecedented victory. I think that the party has rewarded the branches,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketia said the party had moved from the branch elections to the constituency level, where some executives retained their positions while others were replaced. “Then, we came to constituency level. Some were retained, others were not retained. And then, we are now ready to go to the next stage, that is the regional elections,” he said. The regional elections form part of the NDC’s internal reorganisation ahead of its National Congress. The party is expected to elect new national officers, including a successor to Mr Asiedu Nketiah, at the congress scheduled for December 19, 2026.

items.title: GEXIM-backed cashew factory to create 1,500 jobs, boost Ghana’s value-added exports
items.description: Support from the Ghana Export-Import Bank (GEXIM) for the Nadkansco Cashew Processing Factory in Techiman is expected to strengthen Ghana’s agro-processing capacity, expand exports of value-added products and create up to 1,500 jobs. The facility, scheduled for commissioning on November 16, 2026, with President John Dramani Mahama as Special Guest of Honour, highlights GEXIM’s role in financing productive investments aligned with national economic priorities. Ahead of the commissioning, GEXIM Chief Executive, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, said the Bank’s intervention reflected an understanding of the financing needs and operational cycles of agro-processing businesses. “EXIM Bank is here to provide patient capital that understands the work cycle of businesses of this nature,” he said. With Ghana’s cashew purchasing season running mainly from January to June, processors must secure sufficient quantities of raw nuts during that period to sustain production throughout the year. Mr Mensah said GEXIM’s support covered both the establishment of the processing facility and the financing requirements for securing raw materials to ensure uninterrupted operations. He explained that the approach was intended to ensure that investments in machinery and infrastructure were matched with adequate resources to keep the factory operational. The factory has a daily processing capacity of approximately 100 metric tonnes and requires about 30,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts annually to sustain its planned operations. Against Ghana’s estimated annual cashew production of more than 250,000 metric tonnes, the facility represents a significant addition to the country’s domestic processing capacity. Its operations are expected to support the government’s ambition to increase the proportion of agricultural commodities processed locally. Expanding domestic processing will create opportunities to retain more jobs, industrial activity and business income within Ghana while strengthening the country’s participation in international markets for value-added products. Mr Mensah said the investment aligned with President Mahama’s vision of “generating jobs for the people, ensuring value addition, particularly focusing on agro-processing.” Job creation is expected to be a major benefit of the project. The factory currently employs 500 workers, with the workforce expected to increase to 1,500 as operations expand to a full 24-hour production cycle. The recruitment of workers from Techiman and surrounding communities is also expected to extend the economic benefits of the investment to the local population, providing households with employment opportunities and regular incomes. The Managing Director of Nadkansco Processing Limited, Belinda Akorfa Adokpa, highlighted the significant participation of women in the workforce and measures introduced to support working mothers. Women constitute a significant proportion of the factory’s workforce. To support them, the facility has a crèche staffed by trained teachers, allowing mothers to work while their young children receive care. Professional nurses and visiting doctors are also available to provide healthcare support to employees. The project further highlights the commercial opportunities across the cashew value chain. Beyond the processed nuts, cashew shells and extracted oil offer additional commercial uses, while residual materials can be used as fuel for the factory’s boiler. These activities are expected to improve resource utilisation, reduce waste and maximise the economic value derived from cashew processing. With processing already underway, attention will increasingly focus on securing reliable raw material supplies, sustaining production and meeting the requirements of export markets. For GEXIM, the Nadkansco investment demonstrates how development financing can support domestic production, generate employment and expand exports while advancing the government’s objective of securing greater economic returns from Ghana’s agricultural resources through value addition.

items.title: Cap-Vert : Le président sortant José María Neves réélu pour un second mandat
items.description: Le président sortant du Cap-Vert, José María Neves, a été réélu dès le premier tour de la présidentielle du dimanche 15 novembre 2026, avec 63,8 % des suffrages, selon les résultats provisoires. Âgé de 66 ans, il promet de poursuivre son engagement en faveur des libertés et d'une croissance économique inclusive. José María Neves rempile à la tête de l'État cap-verdien. Le président sortant a remporté, dimanche, l'élection présidentielle avec 63,8 % des voix, selon les résultats provisoires. Soutenu par le Parti africain pour l'indépendance du Cap-Vert (PAICV, gauche), il décroche ainsi un second mandat dès le premier tour. Considéré comme favori du scrutin, le chef de l'État a devancé sa principale concurrente, Joana Rosa Amado. L'avocate de 61 ans, ancienne ministre de la Justice et première femme candidate à la présidence de la République du Cap-Vert, a obtenu 31,4 % des suffrages. Soutenue par le Mouvement pour la démocratie (MpD, centre droit), elle a reconnu sa défaite dimanche soir. À Praia, la capitale, José María Neves a réaffirmé ses engagements devant ses partisans. « Les Cap-Verdiens peuvent compter sur moi pour continuer à promouvoir les libertés, la démocratie, l'État de droit », a-t-il déclaré. Le président réélu a également promis de travailler à une croissance « inclusive », avec pour objectifs l'amélioration des salaires et des revenus des familles, ainsi que la lutte contre les inégalités sociales et la pauvreté. Le défi de la participation Cette réélection intervient dans un contexte marqué par plusieurs préoccupations socio-économiques. Le coût de la vie, la hausse des prix des carburants, le chômage des jeunes et les inégalités sociales figurent parmi les difficultés auxquelles le pays reste confronté. L'enclavement de certaines îles et le coût des déplacements entre elles constituent également des défis pour les populations. Autre fait marquant de ce scrutin : la forte abstention, estimée à 68 % selon les résultats provisoires. Sur les 419 448 électeurs inscrits, une part importante ne s'est pas rendue aux urnes. Face à cette situation, José María Neves a évoqué la nécessité de moderniser le système électoral, notamment à travers une éventuelle introduction du vote électronique. Il a aussi appelé les acteurs politiques à réfléchir aux moyens de renforcer la participation citoyenne. Le chef de l'État a, par ailleurs, insisté sur le positionnement diplomatique de l'archipel. « Le Cap-Vert doit rester un espace de paix, un pays qui défend le multilatéralisme, le droit international et la solution négociée des conflits », a-t-il souligné. Un modèle démocratique ouest-africain Situé dans l'océan Atlantique, à environ 600 kilomètres des côtes sénégalaises, le Cap-Vert compte dix îles volcaniques et quelque 550 000 habitants. L'archipel est régulièrement cité parmi les pays africains caractérisés par une stabilité institutionnelle et une alternance démocratique. Dans ce pays lusophone doté d'un régime semi-présidentiel, le président de la République exerce principalement un rôle d'arbitre institutionnel, de garant de l'unité nationale et de la Constitution. Il désigne le Premier ministre en fonction des résultats des élections législatives et représente le pays à l'étranger. L'essentiel du pouvoir exécutif revient au chef du gouvernement. José María Neves, ancien Premier ministre de 2001 à 2016, avait accédé à la magistrature suprême en 2021. Son parcours politique comprend également des fonctions de maire, de député et de président du PAICV. Les résultats définitifs de la présidentielle sont attendus dans un délai de cinq à six jours, selon le calendrier annoncé par la Commission électorale. Avec TV5 Monde Info

items.title: Simandou Mining Summit : la Guinée cherche 1,9 milliard de dollars pour le port de M’Bottiny
items.description: La Guinée cherche à mobiliser 1,9 milliard de dollars pour construire un port polyvalent en eaux profondes à M’Bottiny, au sud de Kamsar, dans la préfecture de Boké. Dans une interview accordée à l’occasion du Simandou Mining Summit, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Bouna Sylla, a détaillé les ambitions du gouvernement pour cette infrastructure destinée à la fois aux exportations minières, au commerce et à l’industrie. Le projet a été présenté aux bailleurs de fonds et aux investisseurs lors d’une table ronde organisée le 13 novembre, en marge du sommet. Selon Bouna Sylla, les études de faisabilité ainsi que les études d’impact environnemental et social sont achevées. Les échanges ont notamment réuni la Banque mondiale, la Banque africaine de développement, la Banque islamique de développement et l’opérateur portuaire Tanger Med. Le ministre a également fait état de l’intérêt de banques privées et de fonds d’investissement. Avec un tirant d’eau prévu de 20 mètres, le futur port pourrait accueillir des navires de type Capesize d’une capacité de 200 000 tonnes. Pour Bouna Sylla, cette infrastructure doit permettre aux producteurs de bauxite de charger directement de gros navires et de réduire le recours aux barges et aux transbordements en haute mer, deux opérations courantes à Boké. « Ce port permettra de rendre également notre industrie de bauxite plus compétitive », a déclaré le ministre. Il estime que le chargement direct contribuerait aussi à limiter les impacts environnementaux et sociaux liés à l’utilisation des barges et aux opérations de transbordement. Un parc industriel inspiré de Jebel Ali Le projet prévoit aussi un terminal à conteneurs, un terminal pétrolier et un parc industriel dans le bassin portuaire. Bouna Sylla cite en exemple le port de Jebel Ali, à Dubaï, et la zone d’activités qui s’est développée autour de lui. Le gouvernement entend s’appuyer sur les liaisons maritimes existantes pour faire de M’Bottiny une plateforme commerciale à l’échelle du golfe de Guinée. Le ministre relève que des navires quittent la Guinée avec de la bauxite à destination de l’Amérique du Nord, de l’Europe ou de la Chine et reviennent à vide. L’idée serait de profiter de ces trajets retour pour acheminer des marchandises et des composants destinés à être assemblés sur place. Bouna Sylla prend l’exemple d’un commerçant de Madina qui se rend aujourd’hui en Chine pour s’approvisionner. Grâce au régime spécial envisagé pour la zone portuaire, ce commerçant pourrait, selon lui, retrouver certains produits en Guinée à des prix comparables, tout en économisant le billet d’avion et les frais d’hôtel. « C’est ce type d’écosystème que nous voulons développer dans notre pays », a résumé le ministre.

items.title: La justicia italiana interviene el banco digital Revolut por sospechas de blanqueo y de operaciones de clanes mafiosos
items.description: La justicia italiana ha intervenido este lunes la sucursal en Italia del banco digital Revolut , el tercero del país pese a operar solo desde hace cinco años, y la tendrá un año bajo administración judicial para subsanar sus deficientes controles de operaciones sospechosas de blanqueo de dinero y de clanes mafiosos. El banco, fundado en 2015 y que ha crecido rápidamente en todo el mundo por las facilidades para abrir cuentas en línea y gestionar actividades de criptomonedas, no está investigado como tal, pero los jueces han ejercido esta posibilidad legal al constatar hasta un millón de episodios de irregularidades en las que la entidad es un tercer implicado por imprudencia o negligencia. “La conducta organizativa de Revolut es censurable”, ha concluido la Sección de Medidas de Prevención del Tribunal de Milán, que considera que no tiene “adecuados controles de blanqueo” y dibuja un escenario de facilidades para actividades criminales. La entidad ha declarado en un comunicado que “colaborará plenamente con las autoridades italianas”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: BoG to scrutinise 2027 budget financing, spending for inflation and exchange rate risks
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) says it will closely examine the financing arrangements and expenditure plans under the government’s 2027 Budget to assess their potential implications for inflation, liquidity and exchange rate stability. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the Monetary Policy Committee will pay particular attention to how government spending and domestic financing requirements interact with monetary policy. Speaking at the opening of the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, he noted that the 2027 Budget comes at an important point in the country’s economic recovery, as government places greater emphasis on productive investment and economic growth. He said the committee would assess the size and composition of the fiscal surplus, its financing arrangements and the potential impact on aggregate demand. “The committee will need to carefully assess the size and composition of the fiscal surplus, its financing arrangements, and the likely implications for aggregate demand, for liquidity, for inflation, and for the exchange rate,” Dr Asiama said. According to the Governor, the timing and distribution of government spending will also be important in determining liquidity conditions within the financial system. He said the MPC would examine domestic financing requirements and their possible effects on monetary conditions to ensure that fiscal operations do not undermine the gains achieved in stabilising the economy. Dr Asiama stressed that coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities would remain critical in sustaining macroeconomic stability. “The objective is to ensure that the fiscal and monetary policy frameworks remain coherent and mutually reinforcing in preserving macroeconomic stability,” he added. The assessment forms part of the Bank’s broader review of economic developments in 2026 and the risks that could shape the country’s monetary policy direction in 2027.

items.title: Exploitation minière : Endeavour Mining présente sa stratégie ESG 2026-2030 à Khossanto
items.description: La Caravane ESG (stratégie environnementale, sociale et de gouvernance) 2026 d’Endeavour Mining a fait étape, vendredi dernier, à Khossanto, après Sabodala, Bransan et Madina Bransan, dans le département de Saraya. L’occasion pour l’entreprise minière de présenter aux populations sa stratégie environnementale, sociale et de gouvernance pour la période 2026-2030. Celle-ci repose sur cinq axes : le développement des compétences, l’accompagnement des communautés, la promotion de l’économie locale, la protection de l’environnement et la gouvernance responsable. La société minière a présenté plusieurs réalisations dans la région. Dans le domaine sanitaire, deux postes de santé ont été construits et équipés à Sabodala, en plus d’une clinique à Bembou et d’une maternité à Diakhaling. Ces infrastructures bénéficient à plus de 10 000 habitants. Cinq ambulances ont également été mises à la disposition des collectivités. A lire aussi : Kédougou : 65 millions de FCFA investis dans la réalisation d’une gare routière Dans l’éducation, plus de 600 millions de FCFA ont été investis dans 41 initiatives au profit de 10 600 enfants et jeunes. Par ailleurs, les achats de fruits et légumes auprès de 15 périmètres maraîchers ont généré plus de 215 millions de FCFA de revenus pour plus de 1 000 femmes et jeunes entrepreneurs entre 2021 et 2025. Sur le plan environnemental, une zone de protection de 1 500 hectares a été aménagée pour préserver l’habitat des chimpanzés d’Afrique de l’Ouest. « Notre ambition est claire : produire de l’or qui apporte une valeur tangible aux individus et à la société », a déclaré le vice-président et chef des opérations, Hassane Hatibu Ally. Le directeur de la performance sociale, Abdoulaye Dramé, a, pour sa part, souligné l’importance de la démarche « On est ensemble », fondée sur le dialogue et la collaboration avec les communautés pour des solutions durables. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Dr. Amo Baffour promises grassroot empowerment fund if voted as NDC Vice Chairman
items.description: An aspirant for the National Vice Chairmanship race of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Dr. Alexander Amo Baffour, is promising the establishment of a Grassroots Empowerment Fund to support party members at the constituency and branch levels. The fund is part of the policies listed by the aspirant as he launches his campaign at Asawase in Kumasi, ahead of the party’s upcoming national congress. Dr. Amo Baffour explained that the fund will provide practical support to the executives to enable them to organise effectively, mobilise supporters and carry out party activities without struggling for resources. He says a party which neglects its base cannot expect to win and retain power, and that his initiative will direct investment into people who work industriously for the party to clinch power. Addressing a crowd of supporters and party faithful, Dr. Amo Baffour is focusing on serving the grassroots, saying he is poised to serve as a “Field Marshal” on the ground to protect the party’s votes and secure victory in the upcoming elections. He insisted the 2028 general election is already a done deal for the NDC, but the real task now, he says, is to plan beyond it. According to Dr. Amo Baffour, his motivation for contesting the National Vice Chairmanship is to help the party break the two-term presidential shuffle between the two major political parties that has defined the Fourth Republic. He said the NDC must not only win in 2028, but go on to win an unprecedented third consecutive term and remain in government well beyond 2040. “My vision is to ensure that NDC will continue to be in government beyond 2040, but without the grassroots this dream can’t become a reality,” he said. The campaign was launched under the theme: “Building a Smarter NDC, Empowering the Grassroots, Delivering Greater Victory”. Dr. Amo Baffour explained that his vision is to help build a smarter, more organised and more responsive NDC that delivers greater victory in every general election. He noted that his vision is the heartbeat of every member of the umbrella family, but warned that it cannot be achieved without serious attention to the grassroots. “Without the empowerment of the grassroots, the base of the party, such a vision cannot be achieved. Elections are won at the polling stations, branches and constituencies, and not in Accra, and that is why the party must invest in, listen to and empower its foot soldiers,” he said. Dr. Amo Baffour was emphatic that the position of National Vice Chairman should not be seen as a retirement post for politicians who are in the dying embers of their political career. Instead, he says, it must be occupied by a candidate who is energetic, visible and always on the ground, connecting with the grassroots and ensuring their voices count in every decision taken by the party leadership. “I will be Field Marshal if elected as Vice Chairman. The Vice Chairman should be active on the ground and connect with the grassroots, making sure that their voices count in every decision that the party leadership will make,” he emphasised. He promised tour to constituencies, engage branch executives, resolve internal disputes early and build a stronger link between the national leadership and the grassroots if given the mandate. Dr. Amo Baffour also announced plans to introduce a Performance Measurement System to reward grassroots members and constituencies that work hard to secure massive votes for the party in elections. He said constituencies that deliver outstanding results must be recognised and rewarded, while those that underperform must be supported to improve. He believes the system will encourage healthy competition among constituencies and motivate those in areas where the party is underperforming will strengthen their campaign strategies. “When hard work is recognised and rewarded, more people will be motivated to work harder for the party,” he said. Dr. Amo Baffour said his campaign is anchored on three pillars: grassroots empowerment, party unity and hard work. He appealed to delegates across the country to vote for him, assuring them that he will not be an armchair Vice Chairman, but a hands-on leader who will work to keep the party united, strong and victorious. “Give me the mandate, and I will work with all of you to build a smarter NDC, empower the grassroots and deliver greater victory in 2028 and beyond,” he said. The launch attracted party supporters from across the Ashanti Region and beyond, with many describing Dr. Amo Baffour’s message as timely and forward-looking.

items.title: Asiedu Nketia credits NDC’s 2024 victory to nationwide branch reorganisation
items.description: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says the party’s decision to reorganise its branches nationwide was a key part of the strategy that helped secure its victory in the 2024 general election. In an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse , Mr Asiedu Nketia said the party moved away from its usual approach after the election and focused on addressing organisational weaknesses at the grassroots level. “We went back to branches and made sure that we did proper branch reorganisation. And to address the challenges that we had there,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketia said the party identified regions where it had struggled electorally and sought to understand the reasons for its performance. He cited the Ashanti and Eastern Regions as areas where the party needed to strengthen its grassroots structures. “There were regions where people thought we were not strong, like the Eastern Region, Ashanti Region, and so on. We identified the cause of our poor performance in those regions and decided to act to tackle those challenges,” he said. According to him, one of the major problems was the absence of functioning party branches in some communities, despite claims by individuals in Accra that such structures existed. “It was mostly because we did not even have branches in places. But people write people’s names to come and mislead us in Accra, and then when we were going to the elections, we would think that we were relying on our branches to select polling agents and so on,” he added. The outgoing chairman said the party responded by deploying experienced organisers to areas where its structures needed attention. He said some of the NDC’s most effective organisers from across the country were brought in to support branch reorganisation in the Ashanti and Eastern Regions. “I’m sure the outcome is there for everybody to testify,” he said. The NDC won the 2024 general election, returning John Dramani Mahama to the presidency. The party has since been conducting branch, constituency and regional-level elections as part of preparations for its National Congress, scheduled for December 19, 2026.

items.title: ‘I don’t wait to be chased out’ – Asiedu Nketia on leaving NDC chairmanship
items.description: Outgoing National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, says he kept his decision not to seek re-election secret, including from his closest friends, until the final stages of the party’s nomination process. In an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse , Mr Asiedu Nketia said he deliberately avoided discussing his plans with others because he feared appeals from friends and party members could pressure him into reconsidering. He said his decision reflected a personal belief that leaders should leave positions on their own terms rather than wait to be forced out. “I don’t wait to be chased out. I always leave when I’m still living. People may say, ‘Oh, he should have stayed longer.’ But life is made up of choices, and I’ve made my choice,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said even his close friends were unaware that he would not contest the upcoming NDC National Chairmanship election. “I knew if I had discussed it with anybody, the type of appeals and other things that will come upon me, they may force me to do what I didn’t want. And so that’s why I kept it to myself. Even my close friends never knew what I’ll be doing,” he said. He added that some people were still calling to ask about his plans on the day candidates were picking nomination forms. “Even on the day of the picking of forms, they were still calling and asking. So it was after 5:00 that they realised that the guy has decided not to contest again,” he said. The outgoing chairman said his satisfaction comes from what he considers improvements made at the party’s headquarters during his tenure. “My satisfaction is that I’m leaving the NDC headquarters better than how I came to meet it. And that is what gives me my satisfaction,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketia has served as NDC National Chairman since 2022, having previously held the position of General Secretary for several years. The NDC is scheduled to hold its National Congress on December 19, 2026, to elect new national officers, including a successor to Mr Asiedu Nketia. His decision not to seek another term brings his tenure as National Chairman to an end, with the party preparing to choose its next leadership.

items.title: New delivery room, kindergarten block brings relief to two communities in Nadowli-Kaleo
items.description: For years, women in Sampina gave birth in difficult and undignified conditions. There was no proper delivery room, no privacy, and little comfort for expectant mothers. In Biire, children aged between three and five had to walk more than three kilometres to Pala every day to attend kindergarten, navigating bush paths and often making the journey in the rain. This week, the stories of the two communities took a positive turn. In Sampina, a new delivery room has been completed at the Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) Compound, while in Biire, a new kindergarten block has been handed over to the community. The two projects are expected to improve access to essential healthcare and early childhood education in the Nadowli-Kaleo District of the Upper West Region. The new delivery room in Sampina was constructed through a partnership between Azumah Resources and the people of the community. While residents provided the labour, Azumah Resources supported the project with materials and other resources. The Member of Parliament for Nadowli-Kaleo, Anthony Mwinkara Sumah, subsequently supported the initiative and joined community members and other stakeholders for its commissioning. The midwife in charge of the Sampina CHPS Compound, who has served the community for three years, expressed relief and gratitude, describing the new facility as a major improvement in her working conditions. “I want to thank our Honourable MP for this good work, with the support of Azumah. We have had several visits from Azumah here, and today, the place is complete. I am very grateful,” she said. Recalling some of the difficulties she encountered while attending to women in labour, she said the poor condition of the former delivery space sometimes made her work frightening. “I remember there are times I come in the night to do delivery, and maybe a lizard will fall, and I will take off running. So if I have a very beautiful place like this, I do not know how to express the joy,” she added. She disclosed that despite the lack of a proper delivery environment, she had conducted 71 deliveries and registered more than 300 clients during her three years at the facility. The District Chief Executive for Nadowli-Kaleo, Mary Haruna, said the new structure represented more than an improvement in healthcare infrastructure, describing it as a symbol of dignity for women and the wider community. “This structure signifies dignity to the women and the men themselves. This structure is an encouragement to women and the people of this community,” she said. She assured residents that the District Assembly remained committed to improving healthcare delivery across the district. “As an Assembly, we are committed to supporting the development of healthcare delivery in this community and the district as a whole. We know maternal mortality will reduce, and then our child healthcare will improve,” she stated. Beyond the new delivery room, residents used the occasion to raise other development concerns, including the lack of electricity in more than 40 communities, the need for staff accommodation for health workers and the completion of their Junior High School (JHS) block. Responding to the concerns, Mr Sumah said the government had plans to extend electricity to all communities in the Upper West Region. He explained that a similar exercise had been completed in the Savannah Region, with the Upper West Region expected to be next. “There is a plan by the government to extend electricity to every community in the Upper West Region. It has happened in Savannah. All the communities in Savannah are now connected to the national grid, and the next region is the Upper West Region,” he said. On the request for staff accommodation, the MP said an assessment would be conducted to determine the necessary support. Regarding the unfinished JHS block, he said the District Chief Executive had undertaken to deploy officers to assess the remaining work and establish what was required to complete the project. For years, young children aged between three and five had to travel to Pala to access kindergarten education, covering more than three kilometres daily through bush paths and often under difficult weather conditions. The Nadowli District Director of Education, Vivian B. Nyekanga, said the situation exposed the children to several risks and made access to early childhood education difficult. “Before the provision of this facility, our little children in Biire faced considerable challenges. They had to travel from Biire to Pala to attend school, exposing them to various risks, including being caught in the rain and other dangers associated with travelling through bush paths,” she said. She said the new kindergarten block would bring relief to parents and provide children with a safer and more comfortable learning environment within their own community. “Today, that story has changed. Through the generosity of our Honourable Member of Parliament, these children can now access education in a safe, comfortable, and child-friendly environment within their own community,” she added. Explaining how the project was initiated, Mr Sumah said it was a community-led effort in which residents provided the labour while he supplied the materials needed for construction. “The community agreed to start a community project, so that I could assist with the materials. From the commencement, it has been the community providing the labour, and then I was providing the materials,” he explained. The MP urged residents to take ownership of the facility by ensuring that children were enrolled and regularly attended school. He warned that the investment would serve little purpose if parents failed to send their children to the new facility. “My plea is that the school now belongs to the community. If you do not bring the kids to school, it is a white elephant. I cannot think of a life now without education,” he said. The completion of the two projects marks an important step towards addressing some of the basic development challenges facing Sampina and Biire. For women in Sampina, the new delivery room offers a more dignified environment for childbirth and improved working conditions for health workers. For children in Biire, the kindergarten block brings early childhood education closer to home, reducing the risks and difficulties associated with travelling long distances to school. Although residents continue to call for improvements in electricity, healthcare accommodation and other educational infrastructure, the two facilities represent meaningful progress in their efforts to secure better living conditions. They also demonstrate the importance of collaboration between communities, public officials and private-sector organisations in addressing local development needs.

items.title: BoG considers changes to monetary policy framework to improve credit transmission
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is reviewing the effectiveness of its monetary policy framework, with particular attention to how policy rate decisions translate into bank lending rates and credit to the private sector. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the Monetary Policy Committee will undertake a comprehensive assessment of the operational framework to determine whether it is effectively transmitting monetary policy signals across the financial system. Speaking at the opening of the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, he said the review would examine the relationship between money market conditions, bank funding costs, lending rates and private sector credit. The assessment is expected to help the central bank identify possible operational constraints and determine whether adjustments to the existing framework are necessary. “The committee has to assess how effectively our policy decisions are transmitted through money market conditions, through bank funding costs, through lending rates, and ultimately credit to the private sector and economic activity,” Dr Asiama said. He said the committee would also examine whether the current operational framework continues to provide an effective policy signal while supporting efficient liquidity management. The Governor expects technical staff to provide detailed analysis of prevailing monetary conditions, liquidity developments and the impact of previous policy decisions. This is particularly important as the central bank seeks to ensure that improvements in macroeconomic stability translate into more favourable financing conditions for businesses and households. Dr Asiama said the review would help the committee determine whether the current monetary policy stance remains appropriate as the economy prepares for 2027. He reiterated that the Bank’s responsibility is to preserve the gains made in restoring price stability and exchange rate confidence while supporting sustainable economic activity.

items.title: Double nationalité en France : Marine Le Pen joue au pompier pyromane
items.description: Après les avoir longtemps dénigrés et mis en doute leur loyauté, Marine Le Pen fait son mea culpa sur les binationaux . À quelques mois de l’élection présidentielle française de 2027, la cheffe de file et candidate du Rassemblement national avoue ses torts concernant la question de la double nationalité . Binationalité : une vieille obsession du Rassemblement national En avril prochain, la fille de Jean-Marie Le Pen se présentera pour la quatrième fois à l’élection présidentielle. Lors des deux premières, en 2012 et 2017, elle avait défendu une position sans ambages et mis dans son programme de campagne l’interdiction de la double nationalité si elle était élue. Elle a néanmoins abandonné la proposition en 2022. Lors de la campagne pour les législatives de 2024, le parti d'extrême droite avait défrayé la chronique et suscité une énorme polémique en proposant d'interdire aux binationaux l'accès à des dizaines de fonctions dans la hiérarchie de l’État. « Il y a des postes stratégiques liés aux secteurs de la sécurité ou de la défense qui sont des secteurs par définition stratégiques. Les réserver aux citoyens français, c’est aussi un moyen parmi d’autres de se protéger de tentatives d’ingérence qui pourraient être orchestrées par des États étrangers », avait expliqué Jordan Bardella, le président du parti. Les Français d’origine maghrébine étaient particulièrement visés, tout le monde l’a compris. La proposition équivaut à exclure de fait des millions de Français. Beaucoup ont été blessés et offensés de voir ainsi leur patriotisme remis en cause pour des gains électoraux. Marine Le Pen sur la binationalité : « J’ai commis une erreur » Tout cela fait partie du passé et procède d’une « erreur », reconnaît Marine Le Pen. Interrogée dimanche 15 novembre sur LCP pour savoir si elle a dit ou proposé quelque chose qu’elle regrette aujourd'hui, elle a répondu par l’affirmative concernant sa proposition d'interdire la double nationalité : « Oui, j’avais proposé la suppression de la double nationalité et c'était une erreur. Je disais à l'époque, si on a une double nationalité, il faut choisir celle qu'on veut garder, soit la française, soit une autre. » La candidate de l’extrême droite a ensuite reconnu que sa proposition a pu léser les Français concernés. « J'ai laissé penser à ceux qui avaient la double nationalité que je nourrissais à leur égard une forme de suspicion dans l'amour ou l'investissement qu'ils pouvaient avoir pour la France. Je pense que j'ai commis une erreur », a-t-elle reconnu. « Je suis revenue sur cette proposition et je pense que j'ai bien fait, parce qu'il n'y a aucune raison évidemment d'avoir la moindre suspicion à l'égard de ceux qui ont deux nationalités, souvent celle du pays où ils sont nés, et celle de leurs parents », a poursuivi la candidate que les sondages donnent gagnante au printemps prochain. Après avoir longtemps joué au pyromane concernant la place des binationaux et plus globalement des étrangers et des Français d’origine étrangère, Marine Le Pen se fait maintenant le pompier qui veut éteindre le brasier qu'elle a elle-même contribué à attiser. À quelques mois de la présidentielle, ce renoncement vise à séduire les Français qui ont la double nationalité. L’article Double nationalité en France : Marine Le Pen joue au pompier pyromane est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Mbacké : conflits agropastoraux, la sensibilisation comme rempart contre les affrontements
items.description: Dans le but de prévenir les conflits entre agriculteurs et éleveurs dans le département de Mbacké, le collectif regroupant les acteurs des deux secteurs a organisé, le 14 novembre 2026, une journée de sensibilisation. Pour venir à bout de ce problème récurrent, les participants ont plaidé pour une révision du code pastoral ainsi que sa vulgarisation auprès des populations concernées. Vice-président du Collectif des éleveurs et agriculteurs du département de Mbacké, Abdou Aziz Sow a d’emblée rappelé que les éleveurs et les agriculteurs sont tous des sénégalais partageant un même espace de travail : la terre. À ce titre, estime-t-il, la paix doit être le maître-mot entre ces deux maillons importants de l'économie nationale. Il invite ainsi chaque acteur à connaître et à respecter ses limites. « Les agriculteurs doivent connaître les limites de leurs champs, de même que les éleveurs doivent respecter les espaces dédiés au bétail », a-t-il expliqué. Pour sa part, l'inspecteur départemental du service vétérinaire de Mbacké, Malick Sall, estime que la persistance des conflits entre les deux catégories d'acteurs s'explique en grande partie par une méconnaissance du code pastoral. Il rappelle que ce texte encadre notamment les questions relatives aux parcours du bétail et que certaines dispositions remontent aux années 1960. « Il y a beaucoup d'arrêtés qui sont aujourd'hui obsolètes », a-t-il indiqué, évoquant également les difficultés liées à l'accès au foncier. « Il n'y a plus d'espace. Donc, vouloir maintenir des parcours déjà définis depuis les années 1960 n'est plus possible », a-t-il soutenu. A lire aussi : Drame de Lompoul : Serigne Ahmadou Badawi Mbacké plaide pour la valorisation de la jeunesse Face à cette situation, il juge nécessaire d'adapter les pratiques agricoles et pastorales aux réalités actuelles du terrain afin de prévenir les affrontements. Dans le même temps, il a salué la mise en place, par le préfet de Mbacké, d'un comité départemental de gestion des conflits. Selon lui, ce mécanisme devrait être étendu jusqu'à la base afin de permettre aux acteurs de faire remonter leurs plaintes et de trouver des solutions appropriées. De son côté, le maire de Kael et secrétaire général de l'Association des maires du département de Mbacké, El Hadji Bâ, a insisté sur la nécessité de vulgariser le code pastoral avant son application. À son avis, certaines de ses dispositions méritent encore d'être débattues avec les acteurs concernés. À défaut, leur mise en œuvre risque de susciter de nouvelles difficultés sur le terrain. Revenant sur la portée de cette journée de sensibilisation, il a regretté l'absence de ceux qui sont souvent directement impliqués dans les dégâts et les conflits, notamment les jeunes. « Ce sont des jeunes qui sont dans les champs, ce sont des jeunes qui sont avec les animaux. Mais malheureusement, ils ne sont pas présents dans ces rencontres », a-t-il déploré. Il estime ainsi que les principales recommandations devraient consister à aller davantage vers ces jeunes, aussi bien du côté des éleveurs que des agriculteurs, afin de les sensibiliser et de les impliquer dans la prévention des conflits. Birane DIOP, correspondant

items.title: Bawumia engages CHAG leadership, pledges stronger partnership to improve healthcare delivery
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has held discussions with the leadership of the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG) as part of efforts to engage key stakeholders on issues affecting healthcare delivery in the country. During the meeting, Dr Bawumia acknowledged the contribution of CHAG to Ghana’s healthcare system, praising the organisation for sustaining its services despite operating under challenging conditions. He highlighted the significant role played by the faith-based health institution, noting that although it operates 42 health facilities, representing approximately six per cent of Ghana’s health infrastructure, it accounts for between 30 and 40 per cent of healthcare services delivered nationwide. According to him, CHAG’s contribution is particularly important in rural communities, where its facilities provide essential medical services to underserved populations, including poor and vulnerable households. He noted that many rural districts depend considerably on CHAG facilities for access to healthcare, making the organisation an important partner in the country’s efforts to improve health service delivery. Dr Bawumia also reiterated the need for a more structured partnership between the government and faith-based organisations, particularly in the education and healthcare sectors. Referring to proposals contained in the NPP’s 2024 manifesto, he said the party recognised the importance of institutionalising collaboration with religious organisations to improve the management and delivery of essential public services. On education, he reaffirmed his commitment to working with faith-based organisations to facilitate the transfer of management responsibilities for mission schools. “My commitment is to partner with them to take over the management of the mission schools,” he stated. He indicated that such collaboration would help strengthen the contribution of religious institutions to education while ensuring that their historical role in the sector is recognised. On healthcare, Dr Bawumia disclosed that discussions with CHAG had focused on the need to review the existing legislative framework governing the association’s operations. He said both sides had discussed amending Act 525 to formally integrate CHAG into the country’s healthcare delivery system, rather than relying primarily on a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to regulate the relationship. The proposed legislative changes, he suggested, would provide a more established framework for cooperation between the government and the faith-based health sector. Rural health workers and medical equipment also discussed The meeting also addressed concerns relating to the conditions of service for healthcare professionals working in rural and underserved communities. Dr Bawumia said the possibility of introducing additional incentives for health personnel posted to rural areas was among the issues discussed. The proposal is intended to encourage healthcare professionals to accept and remain in postings where access to medical services is limited. Another issue considered was the removal of import duties on medical equipment to make it easier for health facilities to acquire modern equipment and upgrade their existing infrastructure. He indicated that the discussions covered several areas requiring policy attention to strengthen CHAG’s operations and improve the wider healthcare system. At the end of the meeting, Dr Bawumia expressed appreciation to CHAG’s leadership for sharing their concerns and contributing to discussions on the future of healthcare delivery in Ghana. He assured the association that the engagement would not end with the meeting, indicating that his team would continue consultations to develop practical policy proposals addressing the challenges facing the organisation and the health sector more broadly. He said further discussions would focus on identifying concrete interventions to improve CHAG’s operations and strengthen healthcare delivery across the country. The engagement forms part of Dr Bawumia’s wider consultations with stakeholders as he considers policy priorities in key sectors, including healthcare and education.

items.title: BoG warns El Niño could trigger food inflation, threaten cocoa export earnings
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has identified the potential impact of an unusually strong El Niño weather phenomenon as a major risk to Ghana’s inflation outlook, agricultural production and foreign exchange earnings in 2027. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says possible weather disruptions across West Africa could affect domestic food production and cocoa output, with implications for prices and the country’s external sector. Speaking at the opening of the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, he said the central bank’s technical team must assess the possible impact of the weather conditions on the domestic economy. “An unusually strong El Niño episode could affect agricultural production across West Africa into the first quarter of next year, with potential implications for food prices, for domestic agricultural output, and for Ghana’s cocoa production and our export earnings,” he said. Dr Asiama explained that the potential disruptions could affect both inflation and exchange rate stability, particularly if reduced agricultural output leads to higher domestic food prices and lower export receipts. He said the implications of these developments must be considered alongside other external uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions, commodity price movements and supply chain disruptions. The Governor noted that although recent developments suggest some easing of tensions in the Middle East, uncertainties in the global environment remain a concern for the domestic economic outlook. The Bank’s assessment will therefore consider how these external and weather-related developments could influence inflation, foreign exchange inflows and the country’s reserve position. The warning comes as the central bank seeks to consolidate recent macroeconomic gains and strengthen the economy’s resilience ahead of 2027.
